author: Shane Burley
title: The movement to defend the Minneapolis 15
content:
This article

The movement to defend the Minneapolis 15

 was originally published by

Waging Nonviolence

.


When Minneapolis organizer Alec Stewart pulled out of his parking spot on June 16 and headed to work, it seemed like an ordinary day. That is, until Homeland Security Investigations, a detective-like sub-agency of Immigration and Customs Enforcement, rolled up with multiple squad cars and dragged him out of his vehicle. 


“I was never told I was arrested,” said Stewart, who goes by Mac. “I was not told what for. I was not shown any warrants. I had no idea [I was going to be arrested] until I was in cuffs.”


Mac was among the thousands of Minnesotans who rallied to defend their neighbors this January when Trump inundated Minneapolis-St. Paul with federal immigration agents who outnumbered regular police 3 to 1. Residents responded with one of the

most sweeping, complex and powerful movements of the decade

, mobilizing a multitude of existing relationships and organizations to craft a shield capable of fighting off Trump’s domestic militia. Using the encrypted app Signal, they built networks to track officers and warn potential arrestees. They launched mutual aid networks to support those who were in hiding to avoid becoming targets of Immigrations and Customs Enforcement, or ICE. They blockaded roads, tailed ICE vehicles and went out on a one-day general strike. 


The charges faced by Mac and his 14 co-defendants, all of whom were arrested on the same day, carry multi-year sentences. The government claims all 15 people indicted “did knowingly conspire … to prevent by force, intimidation and threats, officers and employees of the United States Department of Homeland Security … from discharging the duties of their officers,” while individual defendants have been charged with additional crimes like assault on a federal officer. The alleged “conspiracy” involved everything from conversations in Signal chats about plans to blockade an ICE processing center, to assigning working groups for the Jan. 23 General Strike, to possessing homemade defensive shields or just following federal officers — as tens of thousands around the country have done. 


What’s particularly alarming to the defendants and their allies is that the charges don’t cite any specific officers who were assaulted, and the government’s evidence includes mundane activist chatter: discussing protests and ICE locations, posting an article from the anarchist website CrimethInc. Anything provably tied to organizing, or just radical ideas, became proof of conspiracy: renting a U-Haul, purchasing a trailer from Facebook Marketplace, calling on Facebook for the public to “become ungovernable” — all were alleged evidence of malicious intent. 


Sign Up for our Newsletter


We’ll send you a weekly email with the latest articles.


What’s also alarming is how that information was gathered. Recently, the defense filed a motion that revealed the existence of Operation Puppet Master, a

program to surveil and investigate

 Twin Cities labor unions, churches and community groups in advance of the filing of criminal charges. Unions in which defendants were member leaders had their finances quietly inspected, including their national unions’ political donations. Undercover officers attended protest planning meetings and covertly recorded unsuspecting citizens. The level of surveillance was shockingly broad: Homeland Security Investigations had near carte blanche to categorize almost any organization that could oppose sweeping deportation arrests as potentially criminal. 


If the government can make these charges stick, it could have a profound chilling effect on one of the largest social movements of the 21st century, and could

chart a pathway

 for the Trump administration to effectively criminalize any opposition. That is why these 15 defendants have vowed to fight the charges, and why they have a committee of supporters who are doing what it takes to support those who have been singled out.


They came for everyone


“I think they picked us out because we’re good organizers,” said Treasure Thoreson, a special education teacher who was among those indicted.

All 15 of the defendants are union members

, and many are leaders in their locals. Thoreson is an executive board member of the Minneapolis Federation of Educators and was a captain during their confrontational strike in 2022. When Trump came back in 2024, she knew deportation defense had to be the …

author: Jenny Brown
title: Baristas Ask Organizations to Boycott until Starbucks Signs a Contract
content:
No contract? No Starbucks coffee at the union hall.


Seeking to pressure Starbucks to finally sign a contract with its 12,000 unionized baristas, Starbucks Workers United announced a boycott of the chain August 25. In addition to individual customers, they are asking organizations and unions to

stop patronizing

 the coffee giant, including avoiding catering and sponsorships, until they get a contract.


The AFL-CIO has already signed on, and the 25,000-strong Chicago Teachers Union voted to boycott on August 26.


Starbucks Workers United members conducted their largest and longest strike yet last November, demanding that the company resolve its 550 unfair labor practice charges and negotiate in good faith. Three thousand baristas in 100 cities struck, in some cases staying out  into January. They asked customers to delete their Starbucks phone app and avoid patronizing all stores.


The company seemed ready to bargain for a moment, but then went back to stonewalling, baristas said. “They will continue to stonewall and stall for as long as they believe they can get away with it,” said Campbell Marusa, a five-year barista in Greeley, Colorado.


Sporadic strikes have continued. August 15-16, workers in California, Missouri, Tennessee, and Pennsylvania walked off the job. The walkouts came during Unicorn Frappuccino weekend, when the stores briefly offered a complicated multicolored drink that spiked sales and exhausted workers. Baristas were told they had to work that weekend and could not take time except for emergencies.


In Nashville, baristas walked off August 15 to raise the alarm about a new blending powder the company rolled out in mid-July that became easily airborne and was giving workers sore throats, coughs, and headaches from breathing it.


Starbucks baristas have been fighting for a first contract for nearly five years. Workers started an organizing wave with union election wins in Buffalo, New York, in late 2021. Since then, over 700 stores have voted union—affiliating with the Service Employees’ Workers United division—but that’s still fewer than 5 percent of the company’s 16,000 outlets in the U.S.


To stop the union’s spread, the company has racked up the largest number of unfair labor practices in U.S. history, with 550 still unresolved. Despite well-documented management intimidation, the union continues to grow by several stores a month.


THREE AT ALL TIMES


A key contract demand is around understaffing. Workers are demanding three people on the floor at all times, and they want available hours to go to current baristas, rather than the company’s prevailing practice of hiring more people and keeping established workers starved for hours.


Striking Nashville barista Baylor Baucom told the

Nashville Banner

 that his store sometimes has only two workers. “That’s unacceptable, in my opinion, considering how many different positions we have on our floor—making drinks, making the food, taking orders, taking orders in the drive-through.”


Many longer-term baristas report that staffing has worsened in the last five years. “The working conditions and food service are getting worse while prices are getting higher,” said Marusa. Many workers report that even when they are available to work more, managers keep their hours below the number required to receive benefits.


Marusa said a co-worker in Greeley keeps asking for more hours but is being kept at the minimum. “After asking the manager for more hours, my store manager told her that there are resources to help her budget her money,” said Marusa. “With the hours that she's getting scheduled, she's getting paid less than $800 a month. The issue isn't how she's budgeting her money, the issue is that she is being chronically under-scheduled.”


Pay has improved since the union started organizing, but in 43 states the starting wages are still below $16. The union is asking for $17 an hour starting pay and 4 percent annual raises.


GRUELING PACE, ANGRY CUSTOMERS


Because there is not enough staff for the workload, baristas say they are forced to speed up their work to a grueling pace, while customers face long wait times. Customer frustration is absorbed by the workers.


“Everyone in my store was being scheduled less than their stated preferred hours because of our ‘labor budget,’” said Marusa. Because of this, workers can’t take sick time, lest they drop below the required hours limit.

author: Secretariat
title: On the False Information Concerning the Refounding of the IWA
content:
Earlier this month, the Spanish branch of the International Confederation of Labour (ICL or CIT in Spanish), an international organization that supports integration with Marxist-Leninist and vertical trade unions, published false information claiming that: “The ICL was born from a refounding of the historic International Workers' Association (IWA), following the expulsion of several of its member unions in 2016.”  We refute this information as it is deliberately misleading. The IWA has never voted in favor of its refounding, and such a proposal has never been presented to an IWA Congress for debate. As an international organization based on the principles of horizontalism—that is, decision-making by its members at their Congresses—no decision of this kind could be adopted without going through the IWA's established procedures.


The IWA has clarified this matter on numerous occasions, despite the Spanish branch of the ICL's insistence on perpetuating this falsehood.


The ICL emerged from the efforts of three unions that were formerly part of the IWA. These unions had developed non-organic organizational and leadership structures to join similar organizations, enabling executive action and other practices that did not align with the IWA's tactics and objectives.


By attempting to split the IWA and form another international, refusing to participate organically within it, they effectively excluded themselves and were expelled.


These are some of the decisions of the 26th IWA Congress held in 2016:


"The IWA declares illegitimate any attempts by the disaffiliated CNTE or USI to represent the IWA, to call themselves the IWA, or to 'relaunch' the IWA."


“Any attempts to ‘relaunch’ the IWA, reorganize it, etc., that are undertaken outside the IWA’s established procedures must be considered unofficial and treated as attempts to seize and usurp the International. In any situation where an organization makes a public call for this purpose, a statement must be issued explaining that it is not supported by the IWA. If we become aware that other organizations are being invited to participate, we must inform them that the IWA does not support such initiatives.”


Regarding the “CNT” of Spain: “We can say that the CNT has withdrawn from the IWA, but also that it has disaffiliated itself due to non-payment of dues, violating the IWA’s statutes and attempting to provoke a split.”


These are the IWA’s agreements. Enough with the lies.

"Platform Extractivism: Data Work and the People Powering Artificial Intelligence"

Julián Posada’s upcoming book, titled Platform Extractivism: Data Work and the People Powering Artificial Intelligence, is based on extensive fieldwork among data workers in Venezuela. During the height of the COVID-19 pandemic, amid a hyperinflation crisis, entire communities in Venezuela depended on data work, says Posada, a professor at Yale University. Paid as little as 50 cents per hour and monitored by surveillance algorithms, most workers did not even know who or for what end they were working for. “From the perspective of the worker, you would just see the tasks. … [T]he algorithm here is the manager.”

Julián Posadaco-director of the Computing, Culture & Society certificate at Yale University.

"Platform Extractivism: Data Work and the People Powering Artificial Intelligence"

NERMEEN SHAIKH: We continue our discussion of the hidden data workforce powering artificial intelligence with Julián Posada, author of the forthcoming book Platform Extractivism: Data Work and the People Powering Artificial Intelligence, which is a deep look at data work and data workers in Venezuela. Julián Posada is assistant professor of American studies at Yale University and co-director of its Computing, Culture & Society certificate program.

Julián, welcome to Democracy Now! If you could — we just heard from professor Antonio Casilli about data workers. You focused principally on Venezuela. If you could tell us what you found among data workers there?

JULIÁN POSADA: Yes, so, when I started this project, I actually wanted to focus on Latin America, where I grew up. And the first thing that I found when I started this research is that most of the workers, at the time when I started, around 2020, were located specifically in Venezuela. So, part of the project and the book is about why Venezuela contains so many of the workers that were powering — what I call in the book, “powering artificial intelligence” at the time. In case you weren’t aware, the goal of a boycott is to significantly impact the bottom line of a business to pressure it into stopping some specific harmful behavior.

This means that a disorganized “don’t support this” with no clear timeframe, no clear demand being put forward, and no

organized

 effort to reach the actual customers of the business… is pretty unlikely to achieve anything.

“Boycotts never achieve anything” factoid is actually a statistical error. Historically, boycotts have been an enormously successful pressure mechanism for collective action. Boycotts georg, a social media user who launches a million poorly strategized boycotts every day with no thought given to target selection or actionable demands, is an outlier adn should not have been counted.

author: antimilitarismus
title: She for Him: Ukraine’s Women Leading the Resistance to “Busification” – Marta Havryshko
content:
As the state hunts for soldiers, women in Ukraine are fighting to keep their men from the front.

/ Česky / Românesc / Français / Ελληνικά / Español / Italiano / Русский / український / Magyar /

In recent days, an image of a young woman in Kamianske, in Ukraine’s Dnipropetrovsk region, has ricocheted across social media. She is on her knees before a military recruitment officer, her hands clasped as if in prayer. Her face is a portrait of fear and desperation. His appears impassive.

Her plea could not be simpler: do not take her husband to war.

A woman on her knees, pleading with draft officers not to mobilize her husband and send him to war. Kamianske, Dnipropetrovsk oblast. 2026.

But the officer seems unmoved. He has a quota to meet, and it collides head-on with her desperate appeal. The army needs bodies. Tears and pleas from women on their knees do not figure into that calculus. If anything, they have become an inconvenience.

Today, this woman embodies more than a Ukraine wounded by war—a country bleeding and increasingly desperate for the violence to end. She has also become a symbol of resistance to coercive mobilization, a phenomenon roiling Ukraine in the fifth year of the full-scale war and one that President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s government can no longer easily keep from Western view, despite carefully cultivated narratives of Ukrainian resilience and a willingness to endure the war for “as long as it takes.”

Women are increasingly at the forefront of that resistance.

In Ukraine, coercive street mobilization has acquired its own bitter piece of slang: “busification”—a reference to cases in which military recruitment officers are accused of forcibly pushing or dragging military-age men into vans in public places.

Across videos circulating on Ukrainian social media, women of every generation can be seen intervening as men are confronted by recruitment officers. They film alleged abuses. They publicly shame recruiters for violent conduct. They plead with them to spare husbands, sons, brothers and strangers. And when pleading fails, some fight back—with fists, handbags, shovels, stones, whatever happens to be within reach.

Others shelter men inside their homes, shops and workplaces, blocking recruitment officers from entering and refusing to surrender those hiding inside.

Women have become the face of resistance to busification.

First, women are the primary witnesses to busification.

Ukraine’s streets have increasingly become a female domain. Public transportation can at times resemble a gender-segregated space: the few men aboard might be the driver, an elderly grandfather on his way to yet another doctor’s appointment, or a carefree student still too young to face the draft. Everyone else is a woman.

Women are everywhere because, unlike military-age men, they can still move around the country with relative freedom—without the same fear of being stopped by men in uniform and forced into a minibus. Most women are not subject to compulsory military service. Although roughly 75,000 Ukrainian women serve in Ukraine’s Armed Forces, for most of them military service remains a choice. For men, it is an obligation.

Women fend off draft officers trying to seize a man in Lviv, 2025.

That wartime privilege gives women something increasingly precious in Ukraine: freedom of movement.

And that is precisely why women so often become the first witnesses to episodes of busification—and the first to run to a man’s defense.

Second, women are protecting the men they love.

Their sons. Their husbands. Their brothers. Their partners.

They throw themselves at recruitment officers with the ferocity of animals defending their young from a predator. Mothers shield their sons with their own bodies. Wives wail in the middle of the street as their husbands are bundled into vans, as though they were watching them being carried away to certain death.

Some are so desperate that even pregnancy does not stop them from physically intervening to keep their husbands from being sent to the front.

Others organize. They gather outside Territorial Recruitment Centers and plead for their men to be released. Or rather, they no longer plead. They demand.

“We demand that our men be released! Let fathers return to their children. Return sons to their mothers, and husbands to their wives. We demand an end to these bandit-style abductions of men into captivity.”

That was the message of women who gathered outside a Territorial …

title: 3ήμερο δράσεων για τα 3 χρόνια από την κρατική δολοφονία του Κώστα Μανιουδάκη, 28-30/8
content:
ΓΙΑ ΤΩΡΑ, ΓΙΑ ΠΑΝΤΑ ΚΑΙ ΓΙΑ ΟΣΟ ΧΡΕΙΑΣΤΕΙ ΑΥΤΕΣ ΟΙ ΜΕΡΕΣ ΕΙΝΑΙ ΤΟΥ ΚΩΣΤΗ

Ενημέρωση από τις υποθέσεις κρατικών δολοφονιών του Βασίλειου Μάγγου, του Μοχάμεντ Καμράν και του Κώστα Μανιουδάκη.


Στη συζήτηση θα συμμετέχουν ο Γιάννης Μάγγος, πατέρας του Βασίλειου, ο Αναστάσης Μανιουδάκης, γιος του Κωστή, ο Θανάσης Καμπαγιάννης, δικηγόρος στην υπόθεση δολοφονίας του Κωστή, καθώς και μέλος της ανοιχτής συνέλευσης ενάντια στην κρατική δολοφονία του Μοχαμεντ Καμράν.

title: Gino ne doit pas être extradé ! Rassemblement le 30 août 18h à la Plaine
content:
Le 19 août dernier a eu lieu l'audience de notre camarade et ami Gino devant la cour d'appel de Paris, qui s'est prononcée favorablement à son extradition vers l'Allemagne sous 10 jours.


Il est plus que nécessaire de se mobiliser massivement et de montrer notre soutien de toutes les manières possibles (communiqués de soutien, banderoles, affichages, rassemblements devant les ambassades, etc.) pour éviter à Gino une extradition imminente.


Ne lâchons pas la pression et poursuivons notre travail de solidarité : Gino ne doit pas être extradé.


⁨ ⁨FREE GINO, FREE THEM ALL


Le 19/08 la cour d'appel de Paris a émis un avis favorable à l'extradition vers l'Allemagne de notre camarade et ami Gino. Comme de nombreux.ses antifascistes à travers toute l'Europe, il est pourchassé par la Hongrie, accusé d'avoir participé à une action contre la manifestation néo-nazie du Jour de l'Honneur à Budapest en février 2023.


Alors que la France avait refusé de le livrer à la Hongrie d'Orban, c'est l'Allemagne qui réclame à son tour une extradition. La même Allemagne qui a illégalement déporté Maja, retenu.e à Budapest depuis 2 ans dans des conditions indignes. En Allemagne, Gino encourt jusqu'à 10 ans de prison. Il risque surtout de suivre le même parcours que Maja.


L'Affaire de Budapest est un procès politique dans un contexte où les organisations antifascistes sont considérées comme terroristes en Hongrie ou comme organisations criminelles en Allemagne. La justice française avec cette dernière décision, joue pleinement leur jeu. Derrière Gino, Zaid, Maja et tous les autres, c'est l'antifascisme tout entier qui est attaqué. Nous devons être à la hauteur.


Nous avons peu de temps. Gino a fait appel devant la Cour de cassation. Jusqu'à ce jugement, saisissons chaque opportunité de faire vivre le soutien. Montrons que derrière nos camarades il y a un mouvement. Un mouvement large, un mouvement fort, un mouvement organisé et surtout un mouvement qui ne se laissera pas intimider.


La répression est la meilleure arme des états bourgeois et des régimes fascistes. Ils veulent nous isoler, nous diviser. Tirons notre force de leurs attaques : mobilisons nous, organisons-nous.


Pour s'opposer à l'extradition de Gino, retrouvons nous le dimanche 30 août à 18h à la plaine (place Jean Jaurès) pour un rassemblement unitaire contre la répression !


Ce rassemblement servira de lancement à une campagne d'actions de soutien, du matériel sera disponible sur place !


Contre la répression : solidarité


Liberté pour Gino, non aux extraditions, free all antifas !⁩


Premiers signataires :

Comité antifasciste du 4eme, Antifa Social Club Marseille, Assemblea per il 25 aprile, Riposte Antifasciste, Afroqueer RevolutionR, UPM, Tsedek !, Stop Aux Violences d'Etat, Comité Free El Mahdi Lyoubi, Collectif Al Manba, Marseille Antifas 1er, VISA 13


Communiqué suite à la décision de la cour d'appel


Le 19 août dernier a eu lieu l'audience de notre camarade et ami Gino devant la cour d'appel de Paris, qui s'est prononcée favorablement à son extradition vers l'Allemagne sous 10 jours.


Pour celles et ceux qui ne connaissent pas l'affaire Budapest, Gino est accusé par la Hongrie – avec une dizaine d'autres personnes – d'avoir participé à des violences contre des néonazis en 2023, dans le cadre d'un défilé d'extrême droite organisé chaque année à Budapest en Hongrie : le « jour de l'honneur » qui réunit environ un demi-millier de nazis, commémore l'alliance entre soldats de la Waffen-SS et militaires hongrois lors du siège de l'armée rouge à l'hiver 1945, lorsque la dictature hongroise était l'alliée d'Hitler. Certaines prétendues victimes sont des militants d'extrême droit de nationalité allemande.


Suite à un premier mandat d'arrêt européen émis par la Hongrie, Gino avait déjà été détenu en France plusieurs mois à partir de novembre 2024. Si Gino et d'autres camarades étaient extradés, ils risquaient jusqu'à 24 ans d'emprisonnement en Hongrie. Après une longue bataille, la cour d'appel de Paris avait refusé cette extradition estimant que les risques de jugement inéquitable et de mauvaises conditions de détention étaient trop importants. Notre camarade avait donc été remis en liberté sous contrôle judiciaire.


Le 16 décembre 2025, Gino a été arrêté par les agents de la Sous-direction antiterroriste de la police judiciaire (Sdat) suite à l'émission par l'Allemagne d'un mandat d'arrêt européen à son encontre et placé en détention. Il ressortira deux …

title: Sabaha karşı "Kanlı Ay"ı göreceğiz
content:
Bu yılın en dikkat çekici gök olaylarından biri olan derin parçalı Ay tutulması, 28 Ağustos Cuma sabahı Türkiye'den de görülebilecek. Tutulma saat 04:23'te başlayacak


Ay'ın yaklaşık yüzde 96'sı Dünya'nın tam gölgesine girecek; gölgede kalan bölüm, atmosferden kırılarak geçen güneş ışığı nedeniyle bakır kırmızısı bir renk alacak.


Türkiye'nin tamamı aynı saat diliminde olduğundan, tutulma her yerde aynı saatte görünecek. Ancak o saatte ay batmaya yakın olacağı için en iyi görüş, batı ufkunun açık olduğu yerlerde mümkün olacak. Doğu illerinde ise gün doğumu daha erken olduğu için tutulmanın son bölümü daha aydınlık bir gökyüzünde izlenecek. 


Neden "Kanlı Ay"?


Ay tutulması sırasında Dünya Güneş ile Ay'ın arasına giriyor. Güneş ışığının tayfında mavi dalga boyundaki ışınlar Dünya atmosferinde saçılırken, kırmızı ve turuncu dalga boylarındakiler  atmosferden kırılıp Ay'a ulaşıyor. Bu nedenle gölgede kalan Ay yüzeyi koyu kırmızıya ya da bakır rengine dönüyor. Halk arasında bu gök olayına bu nedenle "Kanlı Ay" deniyor. Dünyanın birçok dilinde de olayın adı aynı. 


Gökyüzü öyküleri |

"Kanlı Ay" eskiden nasıl yorumlanıyordu?


Ay'ın ansızın kızarması, teleskopların olmadığı çağlarda dünyanın hemen her yerinde korku ve merak uyandırıyordu.


Mezopotamya'da kırmızı Ay, hükümdar için kötüye işaret sayılırdı. Bazı Asur ve Babil kralları, tutulma sırasında gerçek kralın yerine geçici bir "vekil kral" oturturlardı, uğursuzluğun onun üzerine gitmesini beklerdi. Tutulma geçince vekil görevden alınırdı.


Anadolu'da ve birçok Türk topluluğunda Ay'ın bir ejderha ya da dev bir yaratık tarafından yutulduğuna inanılırdı; insanlar davul çalar, teneke döver, gürültü çıkararak Ay'ı kurtarmaya çalışırlardı. Benzer inanışlar, Çin'den Balkanlar'a kadar uzanan geniş bir coğrafyada görülürdü.


Kürt halk söylencelerinde Ay tutulması, Ay’ı yutmaya çalışan ejderha ya da dev bir yaratıkla açıklanıyor; yaratığı kaçırmak için bakır kaplara vurulduğu ve silah atıldığı anlatılıyor. Arap halk kültürlerinde de tutulmaya uğursuzluk ve tehlike anlamları yüklenmiş, özellikle hamile kadınlara ilişkin çeşitli korunma ritüelleri uygulanırdı. Alevi-Bektaşi geleneğinde ise Ay ve Güneş güçlü dinsel semboller olmakla birlikte, tutulmaya ilişkin Kürt folklorundaki kadar belirgin ve ortak bir ritüelden söz edilmiyor. 


Mezopotamya Asurîlerinde tutulma, özellikle hükümdar açısından kötü bir alamet sayılıyor; bazı dönemlerde kralı korumak amacıyla “vekil kral” ritüeli uygulanıyordu. Süryani geleneğinde, eski Mezopotamya'daki Ay'ı yutan kötü varlık motifi Süryanice metinlere kadar gelm işti. Ermeniler arasında Ay veya Güneş'i bir ejderhanın yuttuğuna ilişkin halk inanışı yaygındı. Bizans'ta ay tutulmaları, siyasal ve dinsel felaket alameti olarak yorumlanabiliyordu. 22 Mayıs 1453 tutulması, kuşatma altındaki Konstantinopolis'te kentin düşüşünün işareti sayılmıştı.


İnka uygarlığında Ay'ın bir jaguar tarafından saldırıya uğradığı düşünülürdü. İnsanlar hayvanı korkutmak için bağırırlar, köpekleri havlatırlardı.


İskandinav mitolojisinde ise Ay'ı gökyüzünde kovalayan kurt

Hati

'nin sonunda Ay'a yetiştiğine inanılırdı. Ragnarök anlatılarında bu kovalamaca dünyanın sonunun habercilerinden biri olarak yer alır.


(AEK)

title: Francia, antisemitismo e islamofobia: intervista a un attivista di UFJP
content:
Abbiamo intervistato un attivista de l’UJFP (Union Juive Française Pour La Paix) in merito ad alcuni temi all’ordine del giorno: l’antirazzismo e l’islamofobia, l’antisemitismo e l’antisionismo, per approfondire cosa si muove in Francia sul piano delle mobilitazioni e degli avanzamenti della soggettività organizzata su questo dibattito. E’ interessante la critica che il compagno ebreo decoloniale per la Palestina rivolge alla sinistra – istituzionale e non – individuando nella rigidità ideologica uno dei limiti nell’andare nella direzione di un movimento di massa contro la guerra e l’imperialismo.


Daniel è un attivista sindacale e insegnante di liceo nei quartieri popolari nella periferia di Parigi. In quanto ebreo, è anche attivista dell’Union Juive Française Pour La Paix (UJFP). Da tempo si occupa della questione palestinese e della lotta contro il sionismo nell’ambito delle attività sindacali e dei movimenti sociali. In questa intervista analizza il fenomeno dell’imperialismo e del riarmo europeo che si sta delineando sempre più chiaramente sia in Europa che al di fuori di essa. L’intervista è stata svolta a giugno 2026.


Buona lettura!


Mi chiamo Daniel, sono insegnante in periferia di Parigi. Faccio parte dell’Union Juive Française Pour la Paix, che lotta contro il razzismo e contro il colonialismo, per i diritti dei Palestinesi e sono sindacalista nel mio istituto scolastico e con gli insegnanti e il personale della scuola ho partecipato ai movimenti degli ultimi anni come i Gilet Gialli o Bloquons Tout ma anche agli scioperi dei lavoratori.


Come si possono interpretare i legami che diventano sempre più evidenti tra il sionismo e i discorsi politici di destra in Europa, il razzismo, l’islamofobia e l’imperialismo? Oggi c’è stata una rottura con il 7 ottobre e soprattutto dal genocidio massiccio dei Palestinesi ma diciamo che questo si inserisce in una continuità.


Prima di tutto, l’Europa ha sostenuto la creazione di Israele e l’espulsione dei Palestinesi fin dall’inizio, presentando ciò come un processo di autodeterminazione nazionale. Quindi c’è stato un rovesciamento dei valori e si è data la solidarietà a un progetto coloniale.


Questo è stato un atteggiamento permanente da parte delle grandi potenze imperialiste, che si trattasse dell’Europa, della Gran Bretagna, della Francia, della Germania, degli Stati Uniti, dell’URSS. Questo, all’inizio. Poi c’è stato un momento in cui hanno preteso di chiedere agli israeliani di fare degli accordi. Accordi che sono sempre stati ingiusti e sfavorevoli nei confronti dei Palestinesi oltre ad essere stato presentato come colpa dei Palestinesi da parte di Israele. Si parla di Nakba permanente, con una grande espulsione nel 1948, una grande espulsione nel 1967, e ora, molti morti da tre anni. Casa per casa, espulsione per espulsione, in modo permanente. Oggi vediamo un’accelerazione e un’ideologia che viene da Israele, che si presenta come la punta avanzata della civiltà occidentale in difesa di quella che viene considerata un’opposizione musulmana, che riproduce una guerra di civiltà, permeata di islamofobia, di autoritarismo e che trasgredisce tutte le norme di diritto comunemente accettate fino a questo momento.


Quindi ciò che vediamo in Israele risuona con ciò che accade in generale in Occidente, ossia il bisogno delle classi dominanti di entrare in una competizione esasperata che risponde a una sorta di crisi nell’accumulazione del profitto, il che aumenta lo sfruttamento. Per andare in questa direzione ci sono forse due vie, una via che conserva i diritti democratici e un’altra via, puramente di estrema destra fascista, che vuole affrancarsi dalle norme, e che quindi è arrivata al potere con Haider, Orbán, Meloni, Trump — beh, non in Europa ma… Quindi questa estrema destra si ispira a Israele, ma in realtà tutte le borghesie si muovono nella stessa direzione e quindi considerano la solidarietà con lo Stato d’Israele come qualcosa di essenziale. Quindi è vero che, vista questa radicalizzazione di Israele, ciò provoca una radicalizzazione delle classi dominanti occidentali.


Dunque, nel rapporto di dominazione e nella repressione altrettanto duratura rispetto alle colonie, nel rapporto coloniale con altri paesi o con le popolazioni provenienti dalle colonie che abitano le metropoli, c’è sempre stato un razzismo, una stigmatizzazione, un doppio standard nel trattamento. title: «Ангелы в подвалах»: сборник о сирийской революции, написанный местными левыми
content:
Издательский кооператив «Напильник» совместно с исследовательским проектом «Hevale» продолжают распространять уникальную книгу о сирийской революции: «Ангелы в подвалах».

Сирийская революция началась как мирное народное восстание. У неё не было лидеров, партийных структур или внешней поддержки. Люди — молодежь, рабочие, женщины, интеллигенция — вышли на улицы, требуя свободы, достоинства, справедливости. Они создавали местные советы, формировали горизонтальные сети, отказывались от старых моделей власти.

Со страниц «Ангелов в подвалах» говорят те, кто прошёл через тюрьмы режима, осады и изгнание — и не сломался. Их опыт напоминает: будущее не гарантировано — но именно поэтому оно и остаётся возможным.

Стоимость – 1000 рублей, заказать можно через бот обратной связи телеграм-канала кооператива «Напильник».

title: Osman Kavala: Pêkanîna biryarên DMMEyê berpirsiyariya dewleta hiqûqê ye
content:
Osman Kavala di doza Geziyê de cezayê girtîgehê yê muebeta girankirî stendibû. Kavala piştî biryara binpêkirinê ya Daîreya Mezin a Dadgeha Mafên Mirovan a Ewrûpayê(DMME) ku di 25ê Tebaxê de hatibû aşkerekirin, îro daxuyaniyeke nivîskî belav kir.


Ji DMMEyê ji bo Kavala biryara xwe ya duyemîn da: “Divê demildest serbest bê berdan”


25 Tebax 2026


Kavala da zanîn ku biryara DMMEyê vekolîna pêvajoya cezakirinê li xwe digire û bal kişand ser wê yekê ku weke di biryarên berê yên DMMEyê de, di biryara dawî de jî hate teqezkirin ku “bêyî ku delîlên şênber û qanîker ên ku nîşan didin sûc hatiye kirin hebin, mafê azadiyê nayê astengkirin.” Û Kavala weha got:


“Biryara Daîreya Mezin a DMMEyê ya derbarê min de, vekolîna pêvajoya cezakirinê li xwe digire. Di vê biryarê de jî weke ku di du biryarên berê yên DMMEyê de hat teqezkirin ku heke delîlên zelal û bawerker ên li ser kirina sûc tune bin, mafê azadiya jiyanê ya kesekî nayê astengkirin. Di sala 2020an de, di doza yekem a Geziyê de jî dema ku biryara beraatê hat dayîn, ev rastî hatibû nîşandan ku ti delîlek ku nîşan bide min sûc kiriye tune ye."


DMMEyê bi vê biryara xwe ya dawî da nîşandan ku ev nêzîkatî nayê qebûlkirin. Dadgeh nikarin tenê bi nirxandinên giştî yên li ser bûyeran an jî bi texmînkirin û şîroveyên li ser niyet û armanca xebatan biryara cezakirinê bidin.


Kesên ku ti çalakiyek li dijî yasayan nekirine, nikarin rê li ber azadiya jiyana wan bigirin, ev prensîba bingehîn a mafên mirovan e. Parastina vî mafî û pêkanîna vê prensibê li saziyên dewletê, berpirsiyariya dewleta hiqûqê ye ku ji bo welatiyên xwe.


Cîbîcîkirina biryarên DMMEyê jî di bingeha xwe de ji bo pêkanîna vê berpirsiyariyê ye û ji bo vê yekê pêdiviye."


DMMEyê di biryara Kavala/Tirkiye (No. 2) de biryar da ku gelek mafên Kavala yên di çarçoveya Peymana Mafên Mirovan a Ewrûpayê (PMME) de hatine binpêkirin. Dadgehê destnîşan kiribû ku divê Kavala di demeke herî kurt de demildest serbest bê berdan û encamên mehkûmiyeta wî ji holê werin rakirin.

author: Radikal Perspektif
title: Giyotin İş Başında  —  II. BÖLÜM: Marksist Devletin Mutlakiyetçi ve Terörist Mahiyeti
content:
Yazan: Grigori Petroviç Maksimov


Çeviren: Scianus


Çevirilen Asıl Metin


PDF Linki


Paris Komünü’nün demokrasisini savunurken Lenin, onun tam karşısını amaçlıyordu. Ve madem Lenin, kendi kuru ve akademik üslubuyla Marx ve Engels’in eserlerine son derece vâkıftır, o hâlde Karl Marx’ın Mart 1850’de Komünistler Birliği’ne yaptığı hitabede yer alan şu pasajdan haberdar olsa gerek:


“

Demokratlar ya federatif bir cumhuriyet için çaba göstereceklerdir ya da bölünmez bir cumhuriyet olmaksızın yapamayacaklarsa, hiç değilse komünlere ve vilâyetlere mümkün olan en geniş ölçüde özerklik ve inisiyatif tanıyarak merkezî hükümeti zayıflatmaya çalışacaklardır. Buna karşılık işçiler yalnızca tek ve bölünmez bir Alman cumhuriyeti için değil, iktidarın devletin ellerinde en güçlü biçimde merkezîleştirilmesi için de çaba göstermelidirler. Fransa’da 1793 yılında olduğu gibi, komünlerin özgürlüğü, özyönetim vb. hakkındaki bu demokratik gevezeliğin yemiyle kendilerini tuzağa düşürmemelidirler. Günümüz Almanya’sında mevcut iktidarın en güçlü biçimde merkezîleştirilmesini gerçekleştirmek, gerçekten devrimci bir partinin görevi hâline gelmelidir

.”

1


Lenin, “Devlet ve Devrim” adlı broşüründe Engels’in Bebel’e yazdığı mektuptan, şu sözlerle sona eren uzun bir pasaj aktarır:


“

Bizim

2

 devletimiz, mücadele sırasında, devrim içinde, muhaliflerimizi


zor yoluyla bastırmak amacıyla kullanılacak yalnızca geçici bir kurum olduğuna göre, özgür bir halk devletinden söz etmek düpedüz saçmalık olur; mevcut koşullar altında proletaryanın hâlâ Devlete ihtiyacı vardır; ancak buna özgürlük adına değil, düşmanlarını bastırabilmek için ihtiyaç duyar; özgürlük, ancak devletin kendisi varlığını sona erdirdiğinde gündemin konusu olacaktır

.”


Lenin, Rusya’daki “Sosyalist” inşanın örüntülerini işte bu zemin üzerine çizdi ve “Proletarya Diktatörlüğü”nü bu temel üzerinde kurdu. Bunlar, Engels’in öğrettiği üzere, yalnızca proletaryanın düşmanlarına karşı değil, yalnızca kendi muhaliflerine karşı da değil, düşmanlarına karşı yürüttüğü mücadelenin yöntemlerinin hareket noktalarıydı. Lenin “Proletarya Diktatörlüğü”nü şöyle tanımlar:


“

Proletaryanın devrimci Diktatörlüğü, proletaryanın ele geçirdiği ve burjuvazi üzerinde zor yoluyla sürdürdüğü iktidardır; bu, hiçbir yasayla bağlı olmayan bir iktidardır

.”

3


Lenin iktidarı ele geçirdiğinde, hiçbir yasayla kendisini bağlı saymaksızın bu “Proletarya Diktatörlüğü”nü derhal uygulamaya koyuldu. Sol Sosyalist-Devrimcilerin gensorusuna verdiği cevap, ölüm cezasının kaldırılmasına duyduğu öfke ve Sosyalist bir koalisyon hükümeti kurma önerisini reddetmesi, bütün bunların kaynağı aynı yere götürülebilirdi: otokratik iktidar tutkusu; kibir ve ihtirastan doğan, dünyadaki ilk Marksist “İşçi Devleti”ni, kendi Bolşevik Devleti’ni, Engels’in ifadesiyle “Bizim Devletimiz”i kurma girişiminde bulunmaya yönelik yakıcı arzu; yani hakkında şöyle denebilecek bir Devlet:


“ … Devlet biziz, proletaryadır, işçi sınıfının öncü kesimidir.” “ … Devlet —bu, işçiler demektir, işçilerin ileri kesimi demektir; o, öncüdür, biziz.”

4


“Devlet biziz.” … Biz Parti’yiz ve Parti —yani parti ile parti aygıtı— benim. Öyleyse Devlet —benim ve yalnızca benim. Bir Marksist XIV. Louis—siyasal Marksizmin pratikte, yaşamın içinde mantıksal olarak açımlanmasının kaçınılmaz sonucu budur … İşçilerin Sosyalist Devleti, “Proletarya Diktatörlüğü”, bir XIV. Louis tarafından, yani iyiliksever bir despotizm, bir mutlakiyet tarafından taçlandırılmıştır. Bu, kaçınılmaz bir mantıksal zorunluluktur… “Bizim Devletimiz”, yalnızca düşmanlarımızı yok etmek için değil, esas olarak “muhaliflerimizi” bastırmak için kurulmuş mutlakiyetçi bir Devlettir. Ve muhaliflerin sayısı daima düşmanlardan fazladır. Düşmanlar kapitalistler, toprak sahipleri, generaller ve papazlardır. Muhaliflere gelince, bunlar her şeyden önce kolektif “biz”in sınırları dışında duran, yani Parti’nin dışında kalan kimseleri kapsar. “Bizim insanlarımız olmayan” milyonlarca insan, iki muhalif kategorisine ayrılır: kendi düşüncelerine sahip olan, kendi Sosyalist görüşlerini taşıyan ve Sosyalizmi kurmanın yol ve araçları hakkında kendi fikirleri bulunanlar. Çeşitli Sosyalist ve Anarşist gruplar, partiler, işçi sendikaları, kooperatifler, çeşitli dernekler — bütün bunlar doğrudan ve sürekli muhalifler sınıfına girer. Diğer grup ise, yalnızca zaman zaman, aralıklı olarak ve belirli vesilelerle kendi içlerinden muhalifler çıkaran geniş pasif kitlelerden, yani potansiyel muhalifler grubundan …

author: L214
title: Cruauté et infractions à l’abattoir de Perpignan
content:
Entre mai et juillet 2026, des caméras ont filmé ce qui se passe à l'abattoir de Perpignan. Des cochons frappés à coups de poing. Un opérateur qui enfonce son avant-bras dans l'incision de saignée d'un cochon encore conscient. Des moutons balancés par la toison et par les pattes. Des vaches et des moutons découpés alors qu'ils sont encore en vie.

Rien de tout cela n'est accidentel : le couloir des cochons est en angle droit, le box de contention des bovins n'immobilise pas assez les animaux pour un étourdissement précis. Et tout se passe sous les yeux des services vétérinaires de l'État, présents chaque jour d'abattage.

L214 porte plainte pour actes de cruauté et demande la fermeture immédiate de l'abattoir.

Aujourd'hui, vous pouvez agir en une minute en signant la pétition. Merci 🙏

PS : Le 3 octobre à Paris, la Marche pour la fermeture des abattoirs rassemblera celles et ceux qui demandent la fin de l'abattage des animaux !

Les images filmées entre mai et juillet 2026 dans l'abattoir de Perpignan montrent des cochons frappés à coups de poing, des moutons balancés par les pattes, des vaches et des moutons découpés alors qu'ils sont encore en vie.

Ces faits ne sont pas des accidents : les installations, les équipements de contention et les modes opératoires de cet établissement ne permettent pas de respecter la réglementation encadrant la mise à mort des animaux. Ils se produisent chaque jour d'abattage sous le contrôle des services vétérinaires de l'État.

Cet abattoir a été construit en 2015 avec 7,7 millions d'euros d'argent public, et reste dix ans plus tard incapable de tuer des animaux dans les conditions minimales exigées par la loi. Ce n'est pas un cas isolé : c'est la neuvième enquête de L214 en abattoir en deux ans.

Nous demandons au préfet des Pyrénées-Orientales la fermeture immédiate de l'abattoir de Perpignan.

Nous demandons à la ministre de l'Agriculture un audit de tous les abattoirs français, la publication des rapports d'inspection, et un moratoire sur la construction de nouveaux abattoirs : tant que l'État ne fait pas respecter la loi dans ceux qui existent, aucun nouvel abattoir ne devrait sortir de terre.

author: Acratosaurio rex
title: De los mitos, y de cómo quienes los destruyen los crean de nuevo
content:
Así que nos dicen que Durruti era uno de tantos, y a mí me parece que no. Porque a Durruti se le hizo un entierro mogollónico con banda de música, presencia de autoridades, carteles, banderas, una avenida con su nombre... Quienes piensan que los y las anarquistas estamos por encima de esas cosas de los mitos... Me parece que no.

Total que estaba diciendo que por desgracia, los anarquistas tenemos muy pocos símbolos que nos representen, y que Durruti es un símbolo potente que resume en una persona y una frase emocionante, el anhelo de la anarquismo de un mundo nuevo.

Claro, el año 36 dio mucho de qué hablar, y tiene esa Revolución algo que, en fin: que fuimos derrotados por el ejército. Nos dieron la paliza padre, con tanques, aviones, artillería, ametralladoras... Bueno, pues un montón de gente con estudios históricos o sin ellos, se pusieron luego a meditar sobre las causas de nuestra derrota.

Y antes de seguir, aclaro. Estoy hablando de símbolos y de mitos, y de cómo se construyen eligiendo unos datos y omitiendo otros. Y que tal cosa, levantar símbolos y mitos, es inevitable, lo queramos o no. Somos humanos. Los anarquistas también. No somos inmunes. Os lo voy a contar.

Dentro del mundo libertario hay quienes afirman que nuestra Revolución fue derrotada nada más echar a andar, por algo que resumidamente se llama "la traición de los comités superiores". Es decir que nada más tomar Barcelona, la revolución fue abandonada por los "comités superiores del movimiento libertario", salvo contadas excepciones, y acojonados con la movida, en lugar de lanzarse a destruir el Estado burgués, se pactaron con la burguesía. Establecieron un frente antifascista, y las masas revolucionarias, carentes de una organización propia para hacer frente a la traición (en resumen) de los "comités superiores" se ven arrastradas por la vorágine.

¿Cuál es la solución que proponen estos autores para que las masas revolucionarias, no vuelvan a cagarla en el incierto futuro? Pues proponen la creación de comités revolucionarios. Es decir, que a la palabra "comité" se le añade "revolucionario". Y ya tenemos algo que resume, algo que unifica, algo que soluciona. Y he aquí el milagro: cuando un historiador libertario intenta de alguna manera desmitificar el mito de Durruti, acaba creando otro. En nuestro caso, se sustituye a Durruti como héroe individual, por un sujeto colectivo idealizado, que funciona de forma unitaria y coordinada: los comités revolucionarios.

¿Cómo funciona un símbolo a nivel mental? Con Durruti es sencillo: su retrato. Con un "comité revolucionario" es más complejo. De inmediato te trasladas a una habitación y la rellenas de cosas: una mesa, gente sentada, teléfonos, alguien fumando al lado de la dinamita... O sea, tu cerebro transforma una estructura histórica compleja, en una imagen mental del comité relativamente sencilla. Y sí. Hubo comités por miles, sí, y fueron muy importantes coordinando la producción, la distribución, el consumo... Pero al crear como símbolo al Comité Revolucionario, tú haces algo fabuloso: has sustituido el hermoso rostro de Durruti, por una burocracia. Y ambos símbolos siguen siendo imágenes condensadas de una realidad histórica, mucho más compleja...

Eso también depende un poco de cada persona. Yo, por ejemplo, cuando simbolizo a Durruti, me lo imagino sin camisa, musculoso, lleno de pelos, pegando alaridos escalofriantes y golpes de karate acrobáticos, cargándose a un general faccioso y a su escolta. Pero bueno, así soy yo idealizando a Durruti. Otros tendrán otras imágenes.

¿Y qué veo cuando me presentan como herramienta para la destrucción del Estado a un comité revolucionario? Yo veo a unos flipaos hablando en una oficina de lo que deberían hacer los demás. Porque para mí, en mi opinión, la revolución la hace la gente. No los comités. Que son necesarios, sí. Que aparecerán, sí. Que viva el Comité, sí. Pero hasta dónde llega mi experiencia, los comités no son revolucionarios. No.

Y recordad a Durruti, porque no nos asustan las ruinas. Tenemos buenos albañiles.

author: Hassan Alnaser, Mohamed Alagra, Mashair Idris
title: Sudan Nashra: Military strikes RSF convoy inside Chadian territory, sparks regional concerns | Kauda fighting pushes Otoro groups to demand Hilu’s removal from SPLM-N leadership | US proposes nationwide arms embargo on Sudan in Security Council
content:
Subscribe to our Lens on Sudan newsletter

here

.


Washington is pushing in the United Nations Security Council to take the Darfur arms embargo nationwide.


US Senior Advisor on Arab and African Affairs Massad Boulos put the proposal on the table on Monday, after first floating the idea at a council session in June. The draft would expand the 2005 Darfur sanctions regime to all of Sudan, while explicitly bringing drones and related technology under the embargo. The current regime expires in September unless amended or renewed.


Boulos pointed to the growing toll from drone warfare, saying drones accounted for nearly 80 percent of casualties this year and that both sides continue to strike civilians and civilian infrastructure.


Khartoum rejected the proposal outright. Sudan’s ambassador to the UN Al-Harith Idriss said applying the same restrictions nationwide would amount to equating “the state institutions and the rebel militia,” calling the proposal an attack on Sudan’s sovereignty.


Washington has to get past Russia and China, which both pushed back against expanding the sanctions regime and can veto any council resolution. So while the proposal has support from some council members, it is unlikely to go anywhere without a compromise.


Sudan’s drone war crossed its borders twice over the past days.


In western Sudan, military drones struck a convoy of hundreds of Rapid Support Forces vehicles on August 20 inside Chad’s eastern Ennedi region, near the Sudanese border. Two Sudanese military sources said the convoy had been assembled over several weeks at camps in southeastern Libya, and was preparing to enter Darfur through Chad using a new route through North Darfur’s Wadi Howar.


Chad condemned the strike as a violation of its sovereignty and warned that it reserved the right to respond, prompting the African Union to call for restraint and dialogue to prevent a regional escalation. The Sudanese military has yet to comment. 


On the other side of the country, the military said a strategic drone crossed into Blue Nile State from Ethiopian territory and was shot down over Dindro. 


Inside the RSF camp, its main ally in the war and its parallel government, the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-North, led by Abdel Aziz al-Hilu, continues to grapple with an internal crisis that is becoming harder to contain.


Fighting with one of its oldest constituencies, the Otoro tribe, has returned to Kauda, the movement’s political and military center in South Kordofan, with control shifting between the two sides over the past two weeks.


RSF commander Mohamed Hamdan “Hemedti” Dagalo intervened and called for a ceasefire, but overlapping control on the ground made that impossible to sustain. The ceasefire collapsed, and Otoro fighters regained the upper hand in Kauda.


Some Otoro groups are now calling for Hilu to step down and are seeking alliances with other Nuba Mountains constituencies to challenge a political order that the SPLM-N has dominated for decades, but which has increasingly been concentrated in a narrow circle around Hilu, two Otoro leaders told Mada Masr.


And while there is still no end in sight to the war’s battles, Khartoum is preparing to use September’s UN General Assembly in New York to consolidate a post-Khartoum political posture and present its vision for Sudan’s political and institutional order after the war, according to Sudanese diplomatic and government sources informed of the preparations. 


Transitional Sovereignty Council Chair Abdel Fattah al-Burhan remains the leading option to head the delegation. But US sanctions imposed on him in 2025 could make his participation complicated, prompting the government to consider other senior officials if necessary.


The government plans to put its internal political dialogue on the New York agenda. The process, now being hurried in Khartoum, is to be presented as nationally owned, with international actors there to support and facilitate rather than dictate its agenda or outcome.


But a political source close to the dialogue said New York will test the international response to a process whose current, state-curated form is already being rejected by parts of the civilian political camp. 


Sudanese political and civilian forces, opposed to both the war and a military-led political process, rejected Burhan’s call for a dialogue, saying that any process launched while fighting continues — and conducted under military control — would reproduce …

author: Linda Ngari
title: Hybrid Repression: Coordinated Attacks on Rwanda Press Freedom
content:
The paradox of press freedom in Rwanda is that despite the advent of alternative media, younger journalists are more controlled than their older counterparts. “Today’s generation? Yeah, they’re getting more fear than we used to,” 47-year-old Rubens Mukunzi said in a phone interview. Rubens has experienced a Rwanda before Kagame’s 26-year presidency. He was 15 when the genocide that killed at least 800,000 Rwandans happened. The same year that 32-year-old Samuel Baker Byansi was born. While Rubens practised journalism in his home country for 13 years before he fled to America in 2013, Samuel practised for half the time, having started in 2016 and fleeing to Europe in 2022. Rubens had never been arrested for his work even though he earned the name “Mr Bean” from his comic commentary on Rwandan politics through his radio show at the time. But Samuel recalls being arrested more than four times for his work.


In a phone interview, Samuel narrates one of the arrests in 2022 that upended his plans to ask his girlfriend to marry him. “They arrested me for something not serious. I had tweeted that journalist

Kakwenza Rukirabashaija

 fled Uganda. I was detained for like four days. No communication. It disturbed me. I had my proposal that Saturday. I was arrested on Tuesday.” Samuel being arrested for a tweet is indicative of the government’s online surveillance to control free speech and limit the use of social media for political dissent.


Within three months of gathering this report, artist and YouTuber

Aimable Karasira

 was killed (May 6), and Rwandan authorities confirmed the arrest (May 1) of YouTubers Nsanzimana Augustin and Niyonshuti Emmanuel for “suspected spreading of false information” via their

YouTube channel

,

Imbarutso ya Demokarasi

 (The Rise of Democracy). Even though YouTubing is barely profitable in Rwanda since YouTube ads were

suspended

 in 2021. About 10 of the 13 imprisoned Rwandan journalists recorded on the Committee to Protect Journalists’

database

 are YouTubers, illustrating the paradox of press freedom in the country, where the rise of the internet and alternative media has ironically stirred up more repression.


As an early career journalist, Samuel underwent a compulsory civic education programme called

Itorero ry’Igihugu

. A report by Democracy in Africa explains that the programme was

introduced

 in 2009 as part of President Paul Kagame’s post-genocide ideology for the making of a “new Rwandan citizen”, known as

Umunyarwanda.

 Rubens, 30 at the time, was never a student of this programme. Samuel narrates his experience in his

book

 From

Watchdogs to Traitors: The less you know, the more you believe

. “The programme offers certificates symbolizing their support for the RPF. President Kagame holds the honorary title,

Intore Izirusha Intambwe

, a significant figure for all programme participants,” Samuel wrote. In the book, he recounts a time he was arrested for publishing a story titled “Eat and Die: Rwanda Supermarket Selling Toxic Meat”.


Samuel also mentions being offered US$500 by Rwandan authorities trying to recruit him as a government informant. “He [a police officer] expressed the desire to work closely with me in the interest of our country,” he wrote. The offer was backed by enticing dinners at high-end restaurants, free fuel at certain gas stations, tax exemptions, and a get-out-of-jail-free card for the times Samuel violated traffic rules.


 “In the beginning, of course, they don’t recruit you by telling you, ‘You are going to work for us,’ but they come as friends. ‘We want you to be friends with us. We have something to offer, which is a little bit better than what you earn.’  I remember when I bought my first car in Rwanda, and it was supposed to pay taxes of, like, five million Rwandan francs. And then one guy in the police intelligence called the revenue [Rwanda Revenue Authority] and told them, ‘Ah, this is our boy. You don’t need to tax him all this much.’ And just like that, I got my car without any tax paid. It’s like a psychological bribe somehow. So when the same person calls to ask for a favour of talking about someone online, you don’t have the capacity to say no. They give you all those privileges, and they give you this money, but in return you are compromising your own ethics, and this is what they want. But they also want you to maintain your credibility as a journalist, such that when you defend them, it becomes a little bit credible …

author: Abdurahman Nur
title: How Las Anod Changed Somaliland’s Case for Recognition
content:
Somaliland has spent three decades asking the world to trust a specific story about itself: a peaceful, democratic state exercising real authority over the territory it claims, with institutions worthy of recognition. The 2023 war in Las Anod tested all four of those claims — peace, democratic legitimacy, authority over the territory, institutional credibility — within the space of a few months. The war broke the first three claims in the open. What happened next to one critic exposed the fourth.


It began on 26 December 2022 with the

assassination of Abdifatah Abdullahi Abdi

, an opposition politician known as Hadrawi, in Las Anod. Protests followed; security forces fired on demonstrators. On 30 January 2023, before a shell had landed, Somaliland’s Ministry of Information ordered journalists not to publish anything that might worsen the situation. Somaliland authorities later

detained

 and prosecuted journalists for their Las Anod coverage; one, Bushaaro Ali Mohamed, was sentenced that August to a year in prison for “tarnishing the image of state institutions.”


A delegate casts his vote during the electoral process to choose members of the Lower House of the Somali federal Parliament in Baidoa, Somalia on November 25, 2016. UN Photo/ Sabir Olad


On the same day as the Ministry’s directive, President Muse Bihi went on television and blamed the unrest on “terrorists.” Days later,

elders across the Sool, Sanaag and Cayn regions rejected Somaliland’s authority

 outright, and Somaliland’s army answered by shelling the town it claimed to govern.


Amnesty International

 later put the toll at more than 100 dead and 600 injured, hospitals and schools among the buildings damaged, and as many as 200,000 people displaced. No international investigation supported Bihi’s framing. The UN Security Council called for the immediate withdrawal of Somaliland forces and expressed alarm over civilian casualties.


Somaliland’s government described the fighting in Las Anod as a necessary response to a terrorist insurgency by forces seeking to detach territory from Somaliland — a framing that became harder to sustain once SSC-Khaatumo, now the North East State, became a

recognised federal member state of Somalia

. In its view, the events posed an existential threat to the territorial integrity on which Somaliland’s claim to recognition rests. The July 2026 Ministry statement must be read against that background: after losing physical control of Las Anod to the SSC-Khaatumo administration, which has since been recognised by Mogadishu as a federal member state, Somaliland is fighting to retain control of the narrative.


The distinction mattered because the alternative was worse for Somaliland. If Las Anod could be framed as a terrorist insurgency, it remained a security problem. If it was a population inside its claimed territory rejecting its rule outright, it became a legitimacy problem — and legitimacy, not security, is the actual currency of a recognition bid.


No one made that second case with more authority than Dr Markus Hoehne. Two decades of fieldwork had already established that opposition to Somaliland’s rule in parts of Sool, Sanaag and Cayn predated Al-Shabaab by many years, rooted instead in longstanding political marginalisation and rejection of Hargeisa’s authority. During the Las Anod conflict he brought that research into a live international conversation on X (formerly Twitter), documenting developments on the ground as the war unfolded. His earlier work explained why the crisis had emerged; his reporting documented what was happening. Together, they challenged both the government’s explanation of the conflict and the narrative on which Somaliland’s recognition case depends.


The response escalated accordingly. His university in Leipzig received complaints that Hoehne has described as fabricated attempts to cost him his job. On 28 March 2023, Nimco Ali OBE — CEO of The Five Foundation and among the most vocal international defenders of Somaliland’s conduct during the war — tweeted that he was a paedophile “kicked out of Somaliland for abusing girls,” to her then 50,000 followers. Coming from the CEO of a charity built on believing survivors of abuse, the accusation carried a credibility it would not have had from an anonymous account — evidence or not. Weeks later, when the UK and 14 other governments called on Somaliland to withdraw its forces, she dismissed their statement as “rubbish” and said the …

author: ROAPE
title: The murder of Professor Jason Arday
content:
On Sunday 16 August I joined the vigil for Professor Arday in London’s Trafalgar Square in the summer’s heat, packed tight with thousands of protestors marking their respect, holding bunches of flowers aloft, and placards reading, ‘Rest in Power Professor Jason Arday.’ Heads bowed, hundreds around me in tears – the words of his students unbearable, our anger craving a response. 


Professor Arday is dead. Murdered. Yet again another Black person has been killed – pilloried in a public execution orchestrated by a profoundly racist press, and organised fascists.


The vigil spoke to the structural racism that shaped Professor Arday’s life and death. I was struck by British MP Diane Abbott’s comments on the Black experience in the UK and the racism encountered daily. This daily experience is engrained in British institutions, the press and political life.


His family commented about the outpouring of grief and fury, describing their emotions: ‘The public cruelty Jason was subjected to was too much for any man to bear. The outpouring of love, support, and grief since his death means so much to us. Although it is bittersweet now, kindness is needed in life, not just in death.’


Bittersweet indeed – the kindness, support and grief were essential but too late. 


Professor Jason Arday – the Black professor of sociology at Cambridge University – was hounded to his death by a racist campaign to unseat him from his position. In the 22 days leading to his suicide, there were 249 articles in major newspapers in the UK, continual coverage on TV, radio and blogs. This had followed a repeated effort to undermine Arday since he became a professor at the university in 2023.


The noise from this pogrom – accusing him of plagiarism, lies, bombast, academic fakery – was overwhelming. Many people who should have known better joined the chorus. The UK’s mainstream liberal paper, 

The Guardian,

 

launched an investigation into Arday’s scholarship

. I encountered family members who joined in the chorus – denouncing Arday, ridiculing his claims, and his work.


On 5 August, Arday resigned from his post; the following week, on 14 August, he committed suicide. A man described by his students as ‘gentle’, ‘caring’, ‘compassionate’ and ‘inspiring’ was systematically broken – destroyed in a campaign which led directly to his suicide. 


Arday was murdered. 


This was the objective – Arday’s suicide was the logical outcome. Leading the recent crusade was the racist scholar, Nathan Cofnas, who published on his Substack the blog, ‘

DEI Fraud and Cover-Up at Cambridge

’, on 21 July 2026.  A vile man who targeted and conducted his own investigation into Arday’s work  – charging him with plagiarism, which confirmed Cofnas’ thesis that Black people are inferior, unworthy of senior academic positions. 


Cofnas is a symptom of our times. A marginal, bigoted voice that once would have remained largely undetected in the swamp is now amplified by a mainstream, racist agenda. In the global North, these voices have reached fever pitch – finding traction in a political climate that has seen right-wing governments elected, and racist policies normalised in daily political speech. 


To say these developments are worrying is a grotesque understatement – these are clarion signs of our current and deepening crisis, and the irredeemable racism of our political and economic system. This cannot be absorbed and understood simply as a British thing. We see the same tightening of the screw in the personal attacks on International Criminal Court judges and the normalisation of genocide.


There are three observations that I want to make in this piece. Firstly, I want to look at two political parallels –  one that prompted the global mass movement, Black Lives Matter, a few years ago, and the second when antisemitism was denounced by the French author Émile Zola at the end of the 19

th

 century. Finally, I want to say a few things about plagiarism and academia. 


On 25 May 2020 in Minneapolis, George Floyd was stopped by the police, then wrestled to the ground by police officer Derek Chauvin – clips of his slow death over nine minutes were beamed across the planet. Chauvin was later convicted of murder. George Floyd was choked to death by Chauvin, who pinned Floyd to the ground, as he died – filmed by the incredibly brave 17-year-old Darnella Frazie – he was heard saying,‘Mama, mama, mama’, ‘Momma, I love you,’ and ‘Momma! I’m through.’


George Floyd was …

author: AfricanFeminism
title: Recentering African Feminist Epistemologies: A Community of Practice to Prevent and Respond to Sexual Violence
content:
Over the past year, Liberation Alliance Africa has sustained the

Building Knowledge Bridges Community of Practice on Recentering African Indigenous Epistemologies to Prevent and Respond to Sexual Violence

. This Community of Practice is a collective of African feminist scholars, practitioners, organisers, artists, and movement builders committed to the dreaming and making of a world free from sexual violence through knowledge bridges.


Sexual violence continues to impact communities across the African continent, and class, ethnicity and religion play a critical role in making civilians in conflict-affected countries particularly more vulnerable. It disproportionately affects women and girls, and ethnic, gender and racialized minorities. Sexual violence is compounded by conflict, displacement, poverty, and gender inequality. It remains significantly under-reported due to stigma and under-prosecuted? Due to weak and corrupt justice systems. Sexual violence includes rape and sexual assault, sexual coercion and exploitation, including trafficking for sexual exploitation and conflict-related sexual violence such as using rape as a weapon of war. It affects people of any gender and age. 


Our starting premise is simple: sexual violence on the continent cannot be understood, let alone addressed, through frameworks that treat colonialism as history rather than a structural force that continues to shape theory, practice, and response to sexual violence. 


Coloniality was

coined

by Peruvian philosopher and sociologist Aníbal Quijano, and it describes the long-lasting pattern of power produced by colonial rule and shape

s

 how we approach epistemological frameworks through which violence is understood.

Epistemology deals with questions concerning the nature, scope, and sources of knowledge.

 A meaningful analysis of sexual violence must begin by seeking to decolonise knowledge and epistemic structures. This analysis requires us to interrogate the assumptions that underpin dominant theories, question whose expertise is legitimised, and create space for African feminist epistemologies to shape how violence is understood, prevented, and responded to. 


We felt an urgent need to organise as scholars and practitioners to generate new frameworks grounded in our histories, political realities, and lived experiences. Our analyses are rooted in our confrontation of the neo-colonial state, the global imperialist, extractive and patriarchal systems that shape our everyday existence. We arrive as feminists in service of a liberatory project, convinced that knowledge-making is itself a site of feminist struggle. 


As the CoP came together through both intentional convening and organic growth, we began organising our work around three enquiries that we believe are critical to envisioning a decolonial feminist approach to preventing and responding to sexual violence in Africa. 


The first enquiry,

Whose Knowledge? An Audit of the Current Knowledge Systems within Sexual Violence Prevention and Response in Africa

 examines the dominant literature, asks whose voices have shaped the field, whose knowledge has been marginalised, and what becomes possible when African feminist scholarship is placed at the centre of analysis. 


The second enquiry,

 The Coloniality of Sexual Violence: Gender, Power, Sovereignty, and the Neo-Colonial State,

 advances interventions on sexual violence that explicitly interrogate the role and impact of hetero-patriarchal colonial racial-capitalism, alongside the complicity of neo-colonial states, in producing and sustaining conditions of gendered violence. 


The third enquiry,

Truth-telling and Epistemic Sovereignty in the Prevention and Response Continuum

, centres on indigenous and endogenous knowledge systems as essential practice-based frameworks for reimagining prevention, response, healing, accountability, and collective safety.


The Imperative of Recentering African Epistemologies


At Liberation Alliance Africa, we believe African women and gender-expansive people’s knowledge-making and world-building are crucial to de-westernising normative assumptions and dominant approaches. African women and gender-expansive scholars must nurture new ways of knowing and being- knowledge that doesn’t just challenge dominant views, but creates a rich foundation for how we understand reality and tackle life’s critical questions.


For a long time, African women and gender minorities were treated as …

author: Simon Ramapuputla
title: Marikana’s wounds still bleed 14 years after police massacre
content:
Fourteen years after police opened fire on striking mineworkers at Marikana, the massacre is remembered not only for the 34 men who were killed, but for their absence in the lives of their families.


For some, the memory is of a father who never came home. For others, it is the loss of a breadwinner, a brother or a son. And for those who were children when the killings happened, it is the experience of growing up with memories that have become increasingly distant, while the questions about justice remain.


At a commemoration marking 14 years since the massacre, the families, activists and academics reflected on what Marikana means more than a decade later – and on its place in South Africa’s longer history of protest, police violence and struggles for dignity.


For the Socio-Economic Rights Institute of South Africa (Seri), which has represented the families since 2012, the central question remains accountability. Seri secured payments for 35 of the 37 families whose loved ones were killed by police. Two families have received no compensation.


Seri’s executive director, Nomzamo Zondo said the compensation process itself reflected a deeper problem in how the state understood the loss suffered by the families. “Part of that is a narrative that what the state is interested in compensating is the income that the miners would have earned. They do not want to account for the husbands, brothers, sons and fathers that they took away from the families,” she said.


For Zondo, compensation alone cannot address the significance of Marikana. The state also needs to acknowledge that the massacre should never have happened, she argued: “That’s what a public holiday on the 16

th

 of August would mean. It would say: we are saying never, never again.”


She said this was particularly important given the continued use of force by police in managing protests. “We’ve seen that police continue to manage protests through the use of violence. They have continuously refused to accept that their role is to facilitate protests as a constitutional right.”


Zondo also pointed to the failure to implement recommendations made by the panel of experts on public order policing and the management of protests. The panel completed its work in 2018, but its recommendations remain largely unimplemented.


Squalid living conditions in the informal settlement, Nkaneng, in the shadow of Marikana platinum mine, a source of immense wealth for the owners in 2012, Lonmin. Archive photo by The Benchmarks Foundation


Another major concern, she said, was the failure of the National Prosecuting Authority to bring those responsible for the 16 August killings to court. “Every year, of course, when the anniversary comes, there is an explanation that work is being done,” Zondo said. “But now we are like one year short from 15 years since the massacre. We are just 12 years since the Commission finalised its report and recommended that the NPA must investigate and charge whoever is responsible.”


The question, she said, was whether there was “really an intention to hold anyone accountable for the deaths of the 16

th

 of August”.


For the families, however, the consequences of Marikana are not measured only by the progress of criminal investigations or compensation claims. They are lived in the absence of loved ones.


‘I still have that memory’


NowilI Nungu was 15 when her father, Jackson Lehopa, was killed at Marikana. Today, at 29, she remembers him through the ordinary moments of their life together: travelling to school on a bicycle, buying him a Coke and watching him repair the bicycle whenever it broke.


“I have so many memories with my dad,” Nungu said. She was the only girl among six children and had been living with her father in Rustenburg while her mother moved back to the Eastern Cape.


By the time of the massacre, Nungu had moved to the Eastern Cape with her mother. The family did not have electricity and relied on the radio for news. Her father normally called every day after returning from the koppie to tell them he was safe. But that day, he did not call.


Crosses erected at the koppie as a symbol of lives lost on 16 August 2012. Archive photo by Muzi Mzoyi


Sebolai Liau lost his father, the late Janefeke Raphael Liau, at Marikana. For him, the question of justice remains unresolved. “I think regarding the Marikana massacre, there is no justice. I don’t think it will ever be served, but for now it has not been, and there are no signs …
