title: Invasão policial na casa de compas em Porto Alegre (RS)
content:
Na tarde do dia 25 de agosto de 2026 a polícia civil, cumprindo mandato de busca e apreensão, invadiu a casa de um companheiro e uma companheira  anarquistas em Porto Alegre (RS). As forças repressivas estão os envolvendo em uma pixação gritando os nomes de Sara e Sandro na fachada do consulado italiano¹ na cidade.


A incursão policial arrombou portas e apreendeu celulares, HDs externos, pendrives, anotações, cartazes, faixas, livros e latas de spray. Os companheiros não foram detidos, sendo intimados a depor.


As vezes esses pequenos gestos que parecem serem nada, como uma pixação na fachada de um consulado, incomodam aqueles que os anarquistas identificamos como eixos fundamentais do sistema de dominação e controle, as fronteiras se rompem, e mais uma vez a Anarquia incomoda o poder e se manifesta em brotes desde diversas partes do planeta.


Agir em solidariedade, cumplicidade, e responder aos chamados sempre vale a pena porque faz acontecer uma informal e decidida coordenação anarquista internacional.


Pela expansão da revolta.

title: O verbo de fogo de Pedro Augusto Motta (1890-1926)
content:
Por 

Carlos Ferreira de Araújo Júnior

 [1]


Pedro Augusto Motta nasceu no Ceará no final do século 19. Não foram encontradas informações exatas sobre a data e o local do nascimento do libertário, mas, provavelmente, ele tenha nascido entre 1894 e 1895, de acordo com informações dos companheiros libertários de Pedro Motta. Também não foram encontrados dados sobre o local de nascimento, mas sabe-se que o operário viveu e militou na capital Fortaleza por alguns anos antes de mudar-se para São Paulo.


Pedro Motta foi periodista, poeta e tipógrafo. No início, Motta era socialista e foi um dos fundadores do Partido Socialista do Ceará (1919). Logo se converteu ao sindicalismo revolucionário anarquista. O libertário proferiu palestras e ajudou a fundar associações operárias no Ceará, como a Associação Graphica do Ceará (1920), União Geral dos Trabalhadores (1920), Federação dos Trabalhadores do Ceará (1921) e a União dos Trabalhadores Ambulantes de Fortaleza (1922).


Como jornalista, Pedro Motta publicou artigos libertários nos seguintes jornais operários de Fortaleza: A Voz do Graphico (1920-1922) e O Combate (1921). Assinou artigos libertários usando os pseudônimos Atom, Ordep, Vulcano, Plutão, Argos, Argus e Tupan. Motta também fez parte de campanhas libertárias através do Comitê Pró-Flagelados Russos (1921) e do Grupo Libertário Amigos d’A Plebe (1922). Em 1922, Motta lançou o livro de poesias libertárias Verbo de Fogo (1921) [2].


Por conta de perseguições políticas e ameaças contra a vida do libertário, Motta muda-se para São Paulo em 1923. O anarquista cearense logo se junta ao Centro Libertário Terra Livre, na capital paulista, e pouco tempo depois se torna um dos principais editores e redatores do lendário jornal anarquista A Plebe (1917-1951). Um dos primeiros artigos de Pedro Motta no periódico anarquista afirmava que era:


imprescindível a organização sindical anarquista, a fundação de escolas, grupos, núcleos de educação racionalistas, baseadas e regidas por programas delineados nos sãos princípios da grande ideia redentora – o comunismo anárquico. Precisamos, pois, em síntese completa, construir na integridade moral, intelectual e social de cada trabalhador a monumental concepção criadora de toda a Sociedade Futura, que é: DESTRUIR PARA CONSTRUIR.

 [3]


Prisão e deportação


Após a Revolta Paulista (1924), a ira autoritária do presidente Arthur Bernardes se voltou contra todos os militares revoltosos, mas também contra comunistas, anarquistas, inimigos pessoais de Bernardes, capoeiras, etc. Em 1924, Motta e dezenas de libertários foram presos. De São Paulo, o libertário é transferido para o Rio de Janeiro, onde passa meses trancafiado na sede da Polícia Central.


Em maio de 1925, Motta e seus companheiros foram enfiados dentro de uma navio-prisão onde foram obrigados a picar ferrugem. Depois, todos os que sobreviveram foram transportados para Clevelândia, no território do Oiapoque, no extremo norte do país, já na fronteira com a Guiana Francesa. Os anarquistas chamavam o Clevelândia de “Inferno Verde”.


O Martírio no “Inferno Verde”


A Colônia Agrícola de Clevelândia foi criada como um projeto de ocupação e colonização da área, visando a transferência de mão-de-obra nordestina para o local, em plena selva amazônica. Posteriormente, durante o autoritário governo de Arthur Bernardes, o espaço se tornou uma colônia penal, frequentemente definida como campo de concentração, sendo o maior símbolo da estratégia de necropolítica do autoritário Arthur Bernardes.


A colônia penal era abastecida regularmente por navios-prisões, como o Oiapock, o Cuyabá e o Comandante Vasconcellos, que despejavam na colônia penal centenas de presos políticos. Clevelândia foi transformada numa zona de morte para onde eram enviados comunistas, anarquistas, militares rebeldes, capoeiristas, vadios e mendigos. Vários anarquistas brasileiros e estrangeiros foram enviados para o “inferno verde”: Nino Martins, Manuel Ferreira Gomes (português), José Baptista da Silva, Antônio Salgado, Pedro Alves Carneiro, José Alves do Nascimento, José Maria Fernandes Varella, Domingos Passos, Antônio Alves da Costa (Antônio Roux), Domingos Braz (italiano), Pedro Augusto Motta, Biófilo Panclastra (colombiano), Thomas Derliz Borche (uruguaio) e Manoel Nicolau Paradas (espanhol).


Morreram dentro do “inferno Verde”: Nicolau Paradas, Nino Martins, José Maria Fernandes Varella e José Alves do Nascimento. Conseguiram fugir até Saint-George, na Guina …

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: As Meta Agrees to $17B Settlement, Now Is the Time to Regulate AI Before It's Too Late: Amba Kak
content: Prosecutors across 47 states, Washington, D.C., and U.S. territories have announced a groundbreaking legal settlement with technology giant Meta over accusations that the social media company deliberately designed addictive products they knew to be harmful to children. Meta, the parent company of Instagram and Facebook, is set to pay at least $12 billion and up to $17.1 billion in financial penalties, in addition to implementing design changes for underage users. “This is the least they can do to prevent harms that have metastasized and have already caused suicides … [but] we cannot be relying on fines, or certainly even on litigation, after harms have already transpired. What we need are rules of the road. And we need rules that go to the root cause of the business model,” says Amba Kak, the co-executive director of AI Now Institute, who joins us for a wide-ranging discussion on tech policy and regulation. Kak, who advises various governments on AI regulatory guidelines, adds, “The era of looking to tech CEOs or tech luminaries to give us answers for what are fundamentally social and political questions, I think, is gone.”

title: Сослагательное исследование событий как способ рефлексии в интересах лучшего будущего
content:
Рассматривая в ретроспективе историю территорий бывшей Российской Империи с начала 20-го века с анархистских позиций и текущей ситуации, невольно задаешься вопросами: а что бы было, если бы на месте СССР сформировалась анархическая федерация по Кропоткину – как бы она, например, сопротивлялась нападению нацистской Германии? Или как бы пошла "СВО", будь на территории Украины анархическая страна?

Как представляется – войны, также как восстания или революции, являются точками бифуркации (по А. Шубину), в которых определяется дальнейшая история народов и которые можно и нужно анализировать в сослагательном ключе – ведь собственно история продолжается и имеет свойство повторятся с разными степенями отличия.

При этом хаос и дезорганизация и в армиях вторжения, и в госструктурах обороняющейся стороны, хорошо описаны в многочисленных свидетельствах участников и очевидцев этих событий.

Так, в первые годы ВОВ были взяты в плен несколько миллионов советских солдат, что очевидно свидетельствует о неэффективности централизованного бюрократизированного управления и недовольстве политикой большевиков. Несомненно, что несколько миллионов мужчин и тех, кто оказался в оккупации, могли бы при правильной организации, или лучше сказать, самоорганизации и проявлении ими воли свободных людей – могли бы буквально вырезать по ночам всю вторгшуюся армию Вермахта даже кухонными ножами, пользуясь преимуществами личной инициативы и нахождения на своей территории. То же самое можно сказать и о европейских государствах, сдавшихся гитлеровской Германии с 1939 года.

Поразительно, насколько государственные системы лишают воли и просто парализуют огромные сообщества.

Таким образом, начало Второй мировой войны говорит примерно все о государственных системах, которые, будучи не в состоянии сами организовать эффективную защиту от нападения, лишают свои народы субъектности и воли, необходимой для эффективного организованного сопротивления. Единственное исключение – Швейцария – и она является конфедераций с сильным самоуправлением и соответственно выстроенной системой самообороны. Вряд ли получится стопроцентно обосновать, почему именно Гитлер не напал на нее, но сам факт неоспорим.

При этом наличие сильного централизованного государства с обеих сторон только ухудшает гуманитарную ситуацию, нормализуя насилие к своим и военные преступления по отношению к противнику за счет состояния "выученной беспомощности", в котором оказываются целые народы по результатам государственного правления.

На сегодняшний день можно констатировать укрепление украинской государственности по результатам полномасштабного вторжения, и в то же время – затягивание войны, деление на белое и черное, и, что характерно, полное отсутствие даже признаков партизанских отрядов, что говорит о полном подавлении инициативы на местах и безоговорочной победе госструктур.

Оглядываясь на прошедшие годы с начала "СВО", очевидно, что были варианты закончить войну сочетанием политических, военных и дипломатических средств, не уступая притязаниям преступной российской власти.

Сегодня в условиях распространения интернета вполне возможно и необходимо было создать у россиян чувства единения со всем миром – ощущения "мирового гражданства", принадлежности ко всему человечеству и признания российских народов важной частью мирового содружества как в историческом, так и культурном плане. Обеспечение возможности безопасной и комфортной релокации протестных россиян могло изменить ход войны за счет массового дезертирства и упадка потока желающих воевать, а попытки организации новых волн мобилизации властью, очевидно, полностью дестабилизировали бы и армию, и общество внутри страны.

Массового дезертирства солдат РФ через территорию Украины можно было добиться, проводя масштабную информационную кампанию и организуя нормальную жизнь дезертирам в странах Европы. Как показывает практика, для нищего населения из российской глубинки деньги играют в условиях массовой закредитованности огромную роль, раз мужчины достаточно массово соглашаются идти на войну за деньги. Очевидно, что финансовые возможности условного Запада не меньше, чем у российского правительства. Можно было бы попросту перекупать таких "воинов" и их командиров, как это происходило (по некоторым свидетельствам) в ходе свержения режима Саддама Хусейна. Ведь очевидно, что возможность находиться (за примерно те же деньги) в безопасности в странах Запада гораздо привлекательнее, чем умирать в лесополосах Украины непонятно за что. На практике же мы …

author: antimilitarismus
title: Ukrajinské ženy v čele boje proti busifikaci – Marta Gavriško
content:
V posledních dnech se na sociálních sítích rozšířila fotografie mladé ženy z Kamenskoje v Dněpropetrovské oblasti na Ukrajině. Klečí před úředníkem TCC a má ruce sepjaté v prosbě. Na její tváři je patrný strach a zoufalství. On se tváří naprosto lhostejně.

/ Românesc / English / Français / Ελληνικά / Español / Italiano / Русский / український / Magyar /

Žena klečící na kolenou prosí mobilizační úředníky, aby jejího manžela neodváděli a neposílali ho do války. Kamenské, rok 2026.

Její prosba je velmi jednoduchá: neodvádějte mého manžela do války!

Ale vojenský úředník zůstává neústupný. Musí splnit kvótu, a to je v rozporu s její zoufalou prosbou. Armáda potřebuje lidské tělo. Slzy a prosby žen klečících na kolenou do tohoto výpočtu nezapadají. Ba co víc, způsobují jen zbytečné potíže.

Na Ukrajině získala nucená mobilizace na ulicích zvláštní hořký slangový název: „busifikace“ – tak se nazývají případy, kdy jsou mobilizátoři obviňováni z násilného vtahování mužů v branném věku do minibusů na veřejných místech.

Na videích šířených na ukrajinských sociálních sítích je vidět, jak se ženy všech generací zastávají mužů, na které útočí mobilizátoři. Natáčejí na video tyto zneužití moci. Veřejně nadávají mobilizátorům za násilné činy. Prosí je, aby ušetřili jejich manžele, syny, bratry i neznámé muže. A když prosby nepomáhají, některé se brání – pěstmi, taškami, lopatami, kameny, čímkoli, co mají po ruce.

Jiné ukrývají muže ve svých domech, obchodech a na pracovištích, brání vstupu zaměstnancům odvodních úřadů a odmítají vydat ty, kteří se uvnitř skrývají.

Za prvé, ženy se stávají hlavními svědky „busifikace“.

Ulice Ukrajiny se stále častěji stávají doménou žen. Veřejná doprava někdy připomíná prostor rozdělený podle pohlaví: těch pár mužů v kabině může být řidič, starší dědeček, který jede na další vyšetření k lékaři, nebo bezstarostný student, ještě příliš mladý na to, aby byl povolán do armády. Všichni ostatní jsou ženy.

Ženy jsou všude, protože na rozdíl od mužů v branném věku se mohou po zemi pohybovat relativně volně – bez obav, že by je zastavili muži v uniformách a násilím naložili do minibusu.

Ženy se staly tváří odporu proti „busifikaci“.

Většina žen nepodléhá povinné vojenské službě. Ačkoli v ukrajinských ozbrojených silách slouží přibližně 75 000 ukrajinských žen, pro většinu z nich zůstává vojenská služba dobrovolnou volbou. Pro muže je to povinnost.

Tato výsada v době války dává ženám na Ukrajině něco stále cennějšího: svobodu pohybu.

A právě proto se ženy tak často stávají prvními svědky případů „busifikace“ – a prvními, kdo se postaví na obranu mužů.

Zadruhé, ženy brání muže, které milují.

Své syny. Své manžely. Své bratry. Své partnery.

Vrhnou se na mobilizátory s zuřivostí zvířat, která brání svá mláďata před dravcem. Matky kryjí své syny vlastním tělem. Manželky pláčou uprostřed ulice, když jejich manžely nacpávají do dodávek, jako by je před jejich očima odváželi na jistou smrt.

Dnes tato žena zosobňuje něco víc než jen Ukrajinu zraněnou válkou – zemi, která krvácí a stále zoufaleji usiluje o ukončení násilí. Stala se také symbolem odporu proti nucené mobilizaci – jevu, který otřásá Ukrajinou již pátým rokem plnohodnotné války, jevu, který vláda prezidenta Volodymyra Zelenského již nemůže snadno skrývat před Západem, navzdory pečlivě pěstovaným příběhům o ukrajinské vytrvalosti a připravenosti snášet válku „tak dlouho, jak bude třeba“. Ženy se stále častěji ocitají v čele tohoto odporu.

Některé ženy pociťují takovou beznaděj, že ani těhotenství je nezastaví před fyzickými protesty, jimiž se snaží zabránit odeslání svých manželů na frontu.

Jiné se organizují a shromažďují se před územními odvodními středisky (TZK) a prosí o propuštění svých mužů. Nebo spíše už neprosí. Požadují.

„Požadujeme propuštění našich mužů! Ať se otcové vrátí ke svým dětem. Vraťte syny matkám a manžely manželkám. Požadujeme, aby se skoncovalo s těmito banditskými únosy mužů do zajetí.“

Tak znělo poselství žen, které se shromáždily u územního odvodového střediska v Oděse, aby ochránily své manžely.

FOTO: Ženy v Oděse přišly k TCC, aby ochránily své manžely. Rok 2026.

Tento jazyk je důležitý. Tyto ženy nemluví o mobilizaci s použitím zkrášlující slovní zásoby vládních komuniké. Mluví o tom, že jim berou manžely, unášejí syny, že jejich otcové mizí v systému, který, jak se obávají, je nakonec může poslat na frontu. To, co stát nazývá mobilizací, vnímají stále častěji jako násilné odtržení mužů od rodin.

author: Unknown
title: Martyrs turned fear into resistance
content:
They were all there. They shared our emotions and took pride in their people alongside us. Armanç, Şervan, Bêrîvan, Çiya, Berxwedan, Zerdeşt, Argeş, Zilan, and the other heroes were watching us from the skies above the homeland. Meanwhile, at Koşuyolu Park, we listened one by one to their stories on the giant screen, heard their voices, and saw their beautiful faces…


Speaking at a commemoration ceremony for freedom guerrillas who had fallen as martyrs at different times and places in Amed, Çetin Arkaş said: “Our sons and daughters were the most precious children of this people. If the most intelligent and bravest members of a family took on this cause, then know that, thanks to these children, everything will surely turn out well.” Undoubtedly, they were. The force that brought thousands of people into a park for three days and united them as one heart without question was the struggle created by the martyrs.


Ramazan Dengiz, Co-Chair of MEBYA-DER’s Amed Branch, told ANF: “At that moment, the martyrs ceased to be merely the children of their families and became the children of the entire Kurdish people. Everyone saw them as their own children and flocked to the condolence gathering.”


MEBYA-DER, which has organized condolence gatherings for martyrs in different cities across Kurdistan, stood in solidarity with the families and brought people together around the struggle, also managed the three-day commemoration process in Amed with great care. So, what kind of preparations were made to shoulder such a responsibility, how was the situation communicated to the families, and what were the expectations?


Dengiz said: “After the PKK’s 12th Congress, it was announced that ‘we will announce all our martyrs.’ So we were waiting. We were asking ourselves, ‘When the martyrs are announced, how will we receive the news? Will they announce them all together, or how will it happen?’ We were not unprepared.”


25 commissions established


Dengiz said they established 25 commissions both to prepare the families and to manage the condolence process, continuing: “Before sending our commissions to the families, we wanted them to be psychologically prepared and informed about certain issues. We sought help from friends who were experts in this field. When we brought the commissions together, we trained them. Of course, there was tremendous emotion and shock. Once the initial shock had passed, we told them that we needed to establish the condolence gatherings together. It would be the first time that a joint condolence gathering was held in Amed, and we needed a large space. It would not have been possible to accommodate everyone in a condolence house. We set up three tents in Koşuyolu Park. I believe each tent could comfortably accommodate 600–700 people, so we allocated space for more than 2,000 people.”


The people supported the process


Emphasizing that the public embraced the process, Dengiz said: “After the condolence gathering was established, our people flowed into Koşuyolu Park like a river. There was a crowd of a size we had not seen in the past 10 years. We were extremely happy. It wasn’t only the people; civil society organizations, the bar association, and the chamber of industry also provided support. There was tremendous solidarity from places such as Batman, Mardin, Adıyaman, and Urfa. As our families saw such enormous interest and support, the shock they were experiencing gradually began to lift. Our families are already politically conscious families. The feelings of the families and the people became one. Their children ceased to be only the children of their own families and became the children of the entire Kurdish people. Everyone saw them as their own children. Because the people of Amed knew why they had gone, what sacrifices they had made, and what state the Kurdish people had been in before and what stage they had reached now.”


Dengiz said that this organization had not emerged in a single day but was the result of sacrifices made over more than 50 years of struggle: “In the past, it was very difficult to stand by the martyrs. People would fall as martyrs; whether in the mountains or elsewhere, no one could go to them. There was tremendous brutality. But over the past 40 years, a great culture of solidarity has developed, and from our perspective, it has become part of our culture. A culture has emerged. Until now, the state has always used death to frighten us, turning everything into a ‘sociology of …

author: Unknown
title: Teachers launch petition campaign against executions in Iran
content:
The Coordination Council of Teachers’ Trade Unions of Rojhilat and Iran has launched a petition campaign against executions in Iran with the motto “No to Execution, Yes to the Right to Life.” The council called on the public to speak out against executions without fear.


In a statement, the council said that no government, state, or authority has the right over human life, emphasizing that the right to life cannot be subject to the decision of any authority:


“The right to life is the most fundamental and inviolable right possessed by every human being. For this reason, we oppose all forms of execution. Regardless of the charge, we consider the death penalty contrary to human dignity, the right to life, and justice.”


Executions are a tool of revenge for governments


The council described executions as a tool of revenge used by governments, noting that normalizing the death penalty leads authorities to see themselves as having power over citizens’ lives and futures and to make decisions about them.


The statement called on citizens, regardless of their beliefs, political affiliation, ethnic identity, or religion, to support the abolition of the death penalty and changes to Iran’s judicial laws by signing the campaign.


The council also called for alternative sentences to be imposed instead of the death penalty, emphasizing that political activity, freedom of thought and expression, peaceful demonstrations, and demands for civil rights should not be treated as crimes.


The campaign has so far collected more than 600 signatures, with its initial target set at 1,000 signatures.


According to Amnesty International’s annual report, the Iranian regime executed at least 2,159 people in 2025, including 61 women.

author: Unknown
title: Time for democratisation
content:
A board chaired by the Vice President convened and decided to establish a number of subcommittees. One of these is the body previously referred to as the Peace and Political Transition Committee. Renamed the Disarmament and Strategy Committee, Kurdish People’s Leader Abdullah Öcalan will also play a decisive role in this body. As the committee will primarily oversee how the process is implemented in practice, there will be close coordination between the Kurdish Freedom Movement and the committee. A new phase is set to begin in which talks between Imrali and Qandil will intensify.


A political struggle has been underway for nearly two years, with discussions taking place primarily at the political level. The issues debated during this period will now move towards implementation. Although politicians and the media in Turkey speak almost exclusively of disarmament, political steps and disarmament will proceed in parallel. Debating which should come first would mean failing to understand the nature of the process. What is taking place is a transition from a strategy of armed struggle to one of political struggle. Such a transition necessarily requires political change and concrete political steps.


The Kurdish Freedom Movement is not bringing its political mission to an end. It is changing the means and methods through which it pursues its struggle. Can a movement such as the Apoist Movement, with one of the world’s most ambitious ideological and theoretical paradigms, really be expected to abandon struggle? On the contrary, it has undertaken a shift in paradigm and political strategy in order to pursue that struggle more effectively.


Kurdish People’s Leader Abdullah Öcalan’s Peace and Democratic Society project represents the application of this paradigm to the resolution of the Kurdish question in Turkey. Öcalan possesses considerable strength in the fields of paradigm, ideology and theory, while also being a master of practical politics. Paradigms, ideologies and theories acquire meaning and value when they are put into practice. Öcalan has recently emphasised the importance of creative practical politics. The Peace and Democratic Society Process is being pursued precisely in line with this ideological and political approach.


Abdullah Öcalan has brought the process to this point through flexible negotiations, guided by the approach that once a legal step is taken, what follows is a matter of practical politics. From now on, the process will be conducted more transparently, as it has moved from a phase of discussion to one of implementation. The lengthy period of discussions was due to the fact that the issue concerns the political existence of a significant community. The implementation phase will also proceed in line with the discussions held on Imrali. The Kurdish question has been at the heart of those discussions.


Whatever name anyone chooses to give it, it is clear that the issue at hand is the Kurdish question. It is also known that this question stems from an authoritarian system built on denial. The President of Turkey says, “We have put an end to denial.” This means that the Kurds in Turkey were subjected to denial for 100 years. And when their existence was denied, their fundamental rights were denied as well.


Whether this policy of denial has truly ended can therefore be measured by whether the Kurdish people’s freedom of language, culture and identity, as well as their right to govern themselves, are recognised. If freedom of language, culture and identity is still absent, and government-appointed trustees continue to replace elected local administrations, then the policy of denial has not ended. Unless the rights necessary to bring that denial to an end are recognised, the policy itself will continue, and claims that it has been abolished will remain nothing more than words.


If a process of political transition has begun, then political steps must be taken that genuinely bring the policy of denial to an end. The fundamental rights of the Kurdish people must be recognised. In short, Kurds must be brought within the framework of law and legal protection. Only then can Turkey become genuinely democratic. Kurdish People’s Leader Abdullah Öcalan is working towards making Turkey genuinely democratic. This is why he repeatedly emphasises the democratisation of the republic. The republic as it exists today is not democratic and, therefore, is not a true republic. What is now being waged is a struggle …

author: Unknown
title: Ceylan Akça Cupolo: Process must be strengthened with legal guarantees
content:
Criticism and expectations surrounding the bill on “Strengthening National Solidarity and Social Integration,” adopted by a majority vote in Parliament as part of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, continue. Different sections of society are calling for the scope of the legislation to be broadened and for the process to be secured through legal, democratic and transparent mechanisms.


Ceylan Akça Cupolo, a Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) MP for Diyarbakır (Amed), spoke to ANF about public expectations surrounding the framework law.


Cupolo said the law represented an important first step in the Peace and Democratic Society Process, but stressed that its current scope was insufficient. Cupolo also said: “Frankly, as Abdullah Öcalan has also emphasised, we see this law as the first step on that difficult thousand-kilometre road to peace. Yes, we are at a historic threshold. But when we go out and speak to people, we see very clearly just how justified the concerns and criticisms voiced by society are. We, too, are critical of the law’s limited scope. Why? Because the spirit of the law has yet to embrace ‘democratic integration’ and a vision of an inclusive republic.


To put this in concrete terms: in Sur, Bağlar or anywhere else in the region, people need more than broad political rhetoric. They need a genuine social contract that directly touches their lives and gives them a meaningful role in governance. The transition from armed struggle to political struggle cannot be achieved through a declaration of intent on paper alone.”


Parliament must be the primary driving force


Ceylan Akça Cupolo said Parliament must play the central role if the process is to lead to lasting peace. She continued: “To make the process transparent, formal monitoring bodies must be established within Parliament, bringing together the entire opposition, civil society and, in particular, women’s assemblies. We urgently need to implement reforms that will fully open these democratic channels. If we want the Peace and Democratic Society Process to endure, Parliament must be its sole legitimate, transparent and primary driving force.


When we look at the current situation in the Middle East, the regional conflicts in Syria and, in particular, the devastating impact of these crises on women, we understand even more clearly how urgently we need peace and integration within our own society.”


The process must be built transparently


Cupolo stressed that, alongside bringing the century-long grounds for conflict to an end, the democratic Kurdish-Turkish alliance must also be placed on a legal footing. She said their goal was a democratic republic in which everyone could feel a sense of belonging.


Cupolo said: “Our goal is very clear: a ‘Democratic Republic’ in which everyone can feel that they belong. Parliament must assume a constituent role by paving the way for all those who have been excluded and marginalised, particularly women, to participate in shaping a new social contract. Through a Monitoring Board established within Parliament itself, it must carry out this process of construction transparently and in full view of the peoples of Turkey.”


Mr. Öcalan’s working conditions must be guaranteed


Ceylan Akça Cupolo highlighted the role of Mr. Öcalan as the political figure central to resolving the conflict and said: “We must state this very clearly: our most fundamental demand is that Mr. Öcalan, who is the political figure central to resolving this historic process, be provided with legal guarantees for his health, security and the conditions necessary for him to work freely. The progress of the process depends on ending his isolation and ensuring that Mr. Öcalan can maintain uninterrupted contact with society and the political sphere.


The situation of seriously ill prisoners is also among our most urgent and pressing matters of conscience. The ‘right to hope’, a universal requirement of human rights, must immediately be enshrined in law by Parliament.”


Technical and legal work will continue when Parliament reconvenes


Cupolo said their work would continue in the new legislative term, both in Parliament and on the ground, to strengthen the legal foundations of the Democratic Society Process.


Cupolo said: “When Parliament reconvenes, we will not confine ourselves to politics from the parliamentary rostrum. We will continue our technical and legal work without interruption to transform the system towards …

author: Unknown
title: Altan Erkekli: Children of this land must not be made enemies
content:
Actor Altan Erkekli spoke to ANF about the Peace and Democratic Society Process, saying that peace should exist not only in society but throughout every aspect of human relationships.


Erkekli said, “Peace should be an integral part of life. There needs to be peace everywhere. Peace needs to exist in all of our relationships, in our communities, in our families and in the world,” stressing that peace should extend into every sphere of life.


Erkekli acknowledged that it is difficult for everything in the world to coexist in peace. He said: “Because good and evil have always confronted one another since the beginning of the world. But we are a country that has been through many hardships. Those who stood shoulder to shoulder in founding the Republic of Turkey after the Ottoman Empire set out with a principle: to live together in peace on these lands.”


Those who reject division and bloodshed want peace


Erkekli said peace was not something anyone should oppose, recalling Mustafa Kemal Atatürk’s principle of “Peace at home, peace in the world.”


He continued: “Living by this principle is something deeply virtuous and honourable. This is how we were raised from childhood. But over the years, brotherhood, solidarity and unity have been undermined, while many of the actions taken by imperial powers in pursuit of their own interests have been overlooked. From this point forward, however, peace must be established as soon as possible so that these lands are not divided and the world we live in does not turn into a sea of blood.


Amid a region that has become a sea of blood, our ability to stand together in friendship and set an example is extremely important, for this region, for our country and for the strategic position it holds in the world.”


We can overcome pain and resentment through art


Altan Erkekli said that, as an artist, he had made standing for peace a guiding principle in his life. Erkekli said: “In theatre, we were raised to believe in the immense value of a world built on love, peace, labour and friendship. That was also the underlying philosophy of the entire repertoire at Ankara Art Theatre, which I consider my second school. Later, throughout my career, whether in cinema, theatre or television, I tried to be part of works that had something meaningful to say about life. Of course, depending on a channel’s broadcasting policy, there were times when we also appeared in lighter productions, more like soap operas. But in general, I tried to choose work that had something to say about life.


One of those works was the film Güneşi Gördüm (I Saw the Sun). In the film, I played a desperate father in a story rooted in the lived experience of immense suffering in southeastern Turkey. One of his sons is in the mountains, another is a soldier, another has lost a leg, and he is forced to leave after being told, ‘Evacuate this village,’ eventually seeking refuge in another country. I portrayed a man living through profound pain.


One day after the film was released, I was walking down the street and I tell this story because it shows just how precious peace is, when a security guard stopped me at the entrance of a building. He first hugged me and then began sobbing. He said, ‘I really like you, but at first I was angry with you. I thought, what are you doing among these Kurds? Then they practically forced me to go and see this film. I watched it. I’m a nationalist, but I realised that life is not the way it looks from where we stand, and it is not the way we were told it was. You portrayed the pain and helplessness there so beautifully. Why are they making us turn on one another?’


That is the power of art to tell the truth, and I believe it can help us overcome all of this. That is why, as this peace process takes shape, we need art to help overcome the pain and resentment carried in people’s hearts, the pain of grieving mothers, of veterans protesting today, of everyone who has suffered and to create a feeling that can bring people back together through love.


Those who govern, those who live in this country, everyone... There has been suffering. We need to move beyond that suffering, reach out to people and establish peace everywhere. The rights of miners and pensioners must also be upheld, as must those of the people I mentioned earlier who have lost limbs.


We need to be able to say: ‘But all of that is over now. From now on, our children and grandchildren will live in peace in this world, and we …

author: Unknown
title: The ongoing process and the "peasant delusion"
content:
The Kurdish side criticised the “framework law” passed by Parliament on the night of 10 August, arguing that it was insufficient, while at the same time strongly emphasising its historic significance. The law indeed contained serious flaws and shortcomings given the historic importance of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, but it at least brought the war to a halt and opened the way for the parties to engage in politics. As the issue at stake is democratisation and the Kurdish question, both of which have been engulfed in violence for a century, opening the way for politics was undoubtedly of historic importance in itself.


Political activity now appears to be gaining momentum following the President’s signing of the “Law on Strengthening National Solidarity and Social Integration.” The Monitoring and Evaluation Board, the senior body responsible for implementing the law, held its first meeting without delay on 24 August and announced the establishment of four subcommittees.


Although the composition of these committees, how they will operate, and the scope of their duties and powers have yet to be announced to the public, it is clear that the state and the government are taking the work surrounding the process more seriously and seeking to move forward more rapidly rather than allowing it to drag on. Domestic and international political and military developments undoubtedly play a central role in this. Recent statements by the Israeli government and developments in Syria have made even clearer just how critical the process is for Turkey. In domestic politics, it is also evident that taking steps within the framework of the process is necessary for the Justice and Development Party (AKP) government itself. Against this backdrop, public expectations are growing that new and more substantial steps will be taken to implement the law.


The Kurdish side also appears to be increasingly active within the process. For the Kurds, the fundamental condition for progress is undoubtedly that Kurdish People’s Leader Abdullah Öcalan be provided with conditions in which he can live and work freely and directly conduct the process. Both the Kurdish Freedom Movement and the Kurdish people have consistently described this as a red line. The Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) Imrali Delegation has held talks with a number of relevant actors, including the President, and subsequently issued statements. The decision to establish committees aimed at improving Abdullah Öcalan’s working conditions is also regarded as a step that could help pave the way forward. These developments are strengthening a sense of hopeful anticipation on the Kurdish side.


The Kurds, however, are not approaching the process with passive expectation. On the contrary, they are well aware that the Peace and Democratic Society Process is an active process of struggle that must be carried forward by society, and they are seeking to fulfil the responsibilities this entails under all circumstances. Within this framework, political activity and mass mobilisation can be seen increasing across all four parts of Kurdistan. The commemorations of martyrs that have shaped the Kurdish agenda in recent days should also be understood and assessed within this context.


As is well known, it was the heroic struggle waged by the martyrs that brought the Kurds to where they are today. Had it not been for the great struggle carried forward over the past 50 years along the path of martyrdom under the leadership of Abdullah Öcalan, nothing vibrant would remain of Kurdish identity today. If there is now a proud and dignified Kurdish identity, if Kurdish identity lives on and influences those around it, if it has become a valued and rising force that inspires humanity, and if everyone now speaks of resolving the Kurdish question, all of this has been made possible by that struggle and shaped by the legacy of the martyrs.


Well aware of this reality, the Kurdish people continue, as they always have, to embrace their fundamental values and are beginning to develop the process of democratic integration on this basis. By standing by Abdullah Öcalan and the martyrs as the fundamental forces that created these values, they are preparing to take new and stronger steps. Through these activities, they are both broadening the social foundations of the process and laying the groundwork for democratic integration. On this basis, the Kurdish side is also expected to take …

author: Unknown
title: Nathan Jun - Hegel and Anarchist Communism
content:
Author

: Nathan Jun

Title

: Hegel and Anarchist Communism

Date

: 2014

Source

:

Anarchist Studies

, vol. 22, no. 2, 2014, pp. 26–52. <

www.philarchive.org/rec/JUNHAA

>


Abstract


 In this essay, I argue that there are two more or less distinct theories of the State in Hegel. The first, and better known, is developed in the

Philosophy of Right

, wherein Hegel endorses the notion of a coercive, centralised, and hierarchical ‘Ideal State’. This is precisely the theory which certain radical Hegelians of the nineteenth century (e.g., Marx and Bakunin) viewed with such deep suspicion. The second, which has not received as much attention by commentators, appears in the

Phenomenology

 and other early writings. Although this theory introduces many of the key components of Hegel’s later political philosophy, it is nonetheless far more radical in its political implications – most important, in its gesturing toward a society which makes room for the realisation of the stateless, classless vision of anarchist communism. The point is not to demonstrate that Hegel is inconsistent or self-contradictory, but show that there are elements of creative tension within his political theory which are not only sufficient to vindicate him from the criticisms of Marx and Bakunin, but also to re-contextualise him as a radical precursor. As I shall argue, the kind of society that emerges in the final chapters of the

Phenomenology

 need not contain the elements of coercion and class struggle which appear in the

Philosophy of Right

 and repulse Marx and Bakunin. On the contrary, such a society may be understood as prefiguring the classless, stateless society which both Marx and Bakunin ultimately endorse.


 Keywords:

Hegel, Marx, Bakunin, Anarchism


I.


 The most fundamental questions of political philosophy are those which concern the nature and scope of state authority; for example: What is the State and how does it come into being? Does the State possess a ‘right’ to rule which implies a correlative ‘obligation’ to obey? If so, how, and to what extent? The aim of this paper is to explore Hegel’s views on these and other questions pertaining to the State and its authority – questions of obvious importance to Hegel given the sheer volume of exacting and comprehensive analysis he devotes to them. The difficulty, of course, comes in interpreting Hegel’s

answers

 to these questions, which is a famously daunting task.


 Among modern philosophers, Hegel is arguably one of the most resistant to synopsis and circumscription. This explains the proliferation of rival and mutually exclusive interpretations of Hegel’s political philosophy following his death in 1831.

[1]

 As Shlomo Avineri points out, ‘[A]lmost every shade of political philosophy has had protagonists claiming to state its case in what they considered to be a legitimate interpretation or derivative of Hegelianism.’

[2]

 An early example of this phenomenon is the conflict between the so-called ‘Left’ (or ‘Young’) Hegelians and the ‘Right’ (or ‘Old’) Hegelians in the 1840s. Whereas the latter group generally regarded Hegel as an orthodox Christian and a loyal Prussian patriot, the former tended to view him as a bourgeois reactionary.

[3]


 Modern and contemporary discussions of Hegel’s theory are in many respects mere continuations of the earlier conflict mentioned above. In the middle of the twentieth century, for example, some commentators, following the Right Hegelians, viewed Hegel as a monarchist, authoritarian, and/or crypto-fascist who believed, among other things, that Prussia in the 1830s was the actualisation of the Ideal State.

[4]

 More recent commentators, following Left Hegelians such as Bruno Bauer, have tended to see Hegel as a ‘philosopher of freedom’ whose system, if not altogether radical in its own right, nonetheless laid the groundwork for the radical philosophical tradition of the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.

[5]


 Perhaps such disagreements are simply a consequence of the ‘difficulty’ of interpreting Hegel. But there are other possibilities as well. It is possible, for example, to interpret Hegel as having developed a series of distinct and (more or less) incongruous theories of the State rather than a single, uniform theory. Hegel’s mature political philosophy is developed almost entirely in his later writings, most notably – and in some cases exclusively – in the

Philosophy of Right

, and it is possible that these later …

title: Riots in Ukraine: More Than 200 People Attacked Soldiers and Overturned a Recruitment Vehicle.
content:
The incident led to larger-scale clashes with police and soldiers, in which about two hundred civilians took part. The tense situation lasted approximately five hours and continued into the early morning hours of July 9.

Footage broadcast by Ukrainian television showed crowds of people weaving through vehicles in a darkened residential neighborhood, chanting “Shame!” and tearing the uniform off one of the officers. This incident was the latest in a series of attacks on officers at recruitment centers, reflecting long-simmering anger over how the Ukrainian army is filling its ranks.

The incident occurred late in the evening in the Sykhiv district of Lviv on “Chervona Kalina” Boulevard. Officers from the local Territorial Recruitment and Social Support Center stopped and detained a man who was wanted for evading military service. After the detainee was taken away in one of the vehicles, a crowd of about 200 people quickly gathered at the scene and blocked the unit that remained there. The crowd surrounded the service vehicle, smashed its windows, and completely overturned it. The leadership of the Sykhiv District Police Station confirmed that two TRC officers were taken to the trauma unit, but their lives were not in danger.

Video from incident: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=36uxUq0adRU

The incident involving the mobilization patrol triggered an immediate investigation by the prosecutor’s office and the General Staff of Ukraine; officials in Kyiv warn that, in their view, internal clashes are “a weapon of enemy propaganda.” This stance by the authorities is not surprising at all. Whenever anyone rebels against the war effort of their “own” government, the government’s lackeys resort to the argument that such actions aid the enemy.

However, as we can see in similar events across Ukraine, the rioters’ voices clearly express disgust that Russia’s aggression is being exploited to intensify aggression by local authorities, the police, and the military.

Statistics from the Interfax-Ukraine agency show a dramatic increase in tensions in Ukraine: while only 5 attacks on TRC employees were recorded in the first year of the war (2022), there were 341 last year, and since the beginning of this year (2026), the number has already exceeded 100 cases. It should be noted that these figures represent only officially recorded incidents, and it is possible that information about many incidents does not make it into official statistics or media coverage so that the problem of internal tensions in Ukraine can be publicly downplayed.

title: Ephéméride des luttes : 27 août
content:
Le 27 août de l'éphéméride des luttes cherche à frapper au coeur de l'Etat et dans certains cas, elle y parvient. Aujourd'hui, on frappe à la tête, au bras et au ventre


1970 :

 A Milan, dans l'usine Sit-Siemens, on retrouve les premiers tracts signés "Brigades Rouges", ce qui laisse à ce moment-là tout le monde politique et industriel plus ou moins indifférent, chose qui changera considérablement dans les années suivantes.


1975 :

 En Angleterre, début d'une nouvelle phase d'attentats à la bombe lors des 'troubles' : l'IRA fait sauter un bar qui servait de point de rencontre aux gardes à Surrey.


1979 :

 - A Mullaghmore en Irlande, l'IRA fait sauter le "shadow V", bateau de l'amiral Lord Louis Mountbatten, cousin de la reine d'Angleterre, le tuant.


 A Warrenpoint, en Irlande du Nord, l'IRA fait exploser deux bombes, tuant dix-huit soldats de l'armée d'occupation britannique. L'explosion endommage également un hélicoptère de l'armée.


1987 :

 En Corée du Sud, des centaines de grévistes affrontent la police dans deux villes différentes du pays.


1992 :

 En Italie, dans la province de Messina, un pylône d'une ligne à très haute tension est abattu en soutien à Marco Camenisch, anarchiste écologiste prisonnier, libéré cette année seulement.


Pour en apprendre plus, et si vous voulez lui écrire, vous pouvez le trouver chez nos camarades de

Renversé

.


2015 :

 A Louvain en Belgique, un incendie volontaire se déclenche contre un centre de recherches en nanotechnologies et en technologie chimique.


Voir

l'éphéméride anarchiste

 du 27 août.

title: Kevin Tucker - Society Without Strangers
content:
Author

: Kevin Tucker

Title

: Society Without Strangers

Subtitle

: Conflict Resolution, Domestication and Systemic Violence

Date

: 2016

Source

: Black and Green Review, No. 4. <

www.archive.org/details/bagr-4

>


Sahlins has called the state a society especially constituted to maintain law and order. The vast administrative hierarchies of the state are, of course, absent in band and tribal societies. An alternative but complementary view is to regard the process of social evolution leading to the state as one of

 externalizing

violence rather than

 controlling

or

 eliminating

it. Such a view enables us to see the evolution of social control in a different light.


 —Richard Lee,

The !Kung San

[1]


 /Twi was a dangerous man.


 Living amongst the /Du/da clan of the nomadic foraging !Kung San of Namibia of 1940s, /Twi stood out. Violence amongst the indisputably egalitarian !Kung has been both well-documented and largely over-stated. But /Twi was particularly violent. By his own family’s telling, he was possibly psychotic.


 Amongst his contemporary !Kung this was well known.


 Fed up, /Xashe, another !Kung man at /Du/da, one day ambushed /Twi, shooting him in the hip with a poisoned arrow, their preferred hunting weapon. They grappled and /Xashe’s mother-in-law held / Twi and told /Xashe to run. Other residents at the camp gathered around /Twi as he pulled the arrow from his hip. Some tried helping him by cutting the wound and attempt extracting the poison out.


 /Twi took advantage of the situation. He snapped. He flung a spear which ripped the cheek of a woman named //Kushe. //Kushe’s husband, N!eishi, came to her aid and /Twi shot him in the back with a poisoned arrow.


 At this point, everyone took cover, shooting arrows back at /Twi.


 None sought to give aid to /Twi. They had decided, collectively, that he had to die.


 /Twi walked out to the center of the camp and sat, calling out, “are you still afraid of me? Well I am finished, I have no more breath. Come here and kill me… Do you fear my weapons? Here I am putting them out of reach. I won’t touch them. Come kill me.” As /Twi’s younger brother, ≠Toma, recalled:


Then they all fired on him with poisoned arrows till he looked like a porcupine. Then he lay flat. All approached him, men and women, and stabbed his body with spears even after he was dead.


 /Twi was buried and the camp split up. All going their separate ways.

[2]


Within civilization, we have a very strange relationship with violence. For anthropologists Nancy Scheper-Hughes and Philippe Bourgois violence “defies easy categorization. It can be everything and nothing; legitimate or illegitimate; visible or invisible; necessary or useless; senseless and gratuitous or utterly rational and strategic.” It is a small term for a range of actions and provocations.


 In their summation, “violence is in the eye of the beholder.”

[3]

 You know it when you see or experience it.


 Violence is an outburst. It is a response to emotions, to anger, and to fear.


 As animals, violence has a place.


 As animals, violence also has its thresholds.


 When we remove the distance between our lives and our actions: violence is just one part of our experience of the world. It is a trait, an ability, but hardly one that defines our existence. In the civilized perceptions of the world,

nature

 is a passive place.

[4]

 For the escapist backpacker or the spiritual zealot, wilderness is a place of peaceful reflection. We carry these voyeuristic perceptions of the world, of the ecology of life, because they are comforting. On a surface level they stand in stark contrast to the systemic, organized violence and anxiety of civilized life.


 As technology intrudes, this contrast only becomes louder.


 Our perception of wildness echoes our understanding of what it means to be an animal, of what it means to be human. Embracing that wildness is neither a simple nor an easy process, but it gives us the ability to know who we are, what we need, and what stands between us.


 Wildness is a state where passivity is not an option. To borrow a phrase from Tamarack Song, wildness is a state of

dynamic tension

.

[5]

 In this all beings are aware, ready, and reliant on the songs of birds, the movement of leaves, the sounds of the environment. Here we inhabit a state that is neither entirely peaceful nor warring, but of

being

. This is a place where humans are neither angels nor demons. This is a …

author: Andrés
title: Recuperar las huellas del lodo. Se presenta la parte III de El pecho en la ruta
content:
El próximo miércoles 09 de septiembre se presenta la tercera parte de

El pecho en la ruta. Las organizaciones piqueteras y territoriales durante el primer gobierno kirchnerista

(2003-2007). Su autor, Nicolás Guillermo Salas, milita desde 2010 en el Frente de Organizaciones en Lucha (FOL). Es testigo y parte de organizaciones de base, sobre las que viene escribiendo desde hace más de 6 años de manera sistemática, en un círculo de tareas consistentes en participar, observar, estudiar, investigar, entrevistar, leer. Y cuestionar. Porque

analiza

sin complacencias el derrotero, sus referentes más visibles, los acuerdos programados, las renuncias, los bandazos. Los dos primeros volúmenes abordaron la complejidad de la que emergieron los movimientos sociales y su desarrollo a través del tiempo. En este, hace foco sobre las organizaciones piqueteras y territoriales al calor del primer gobierno kirchnerista (2003-2007). Los tres tomos dan cuenta de la profundidad de una investigación que avanza sobre la solidez de una prosa clara, pulida, ágil. Y han sido editados en trabajo conjunto de ANRed y Legüero, mientras que para esta última parte se sumó La Caldera, el joven sello editorial de Marabunta.

Por Andrés Manrique (ANRed).


El pecho en la ruta: Las organizaciones piqueteras y territoriales durante el primer gobierno kirchnerista (2003-2007)


La tercera parte de

El pecho en la ruta

 se presentará en los próximos días. A lo largo del volumen de 396 páginas, 230 entradas bibliográficas y decenas de entrevistas se reconstruye exhaustivamente una época que fue mutando. Y que no cesa. El modo en que su autor articula fuentes periodísticas, entrevistas realizadas para el libro y bibliografías de origen diverso (CELS, prensas de agrupaciones, de sindicatos, de organismos) a través de estos últimos veinte años, permite que nos asomemos a un campo importante de disputas político territoriales fundamental en la historia reciente de nuestro país.


Lo que pasó hace poco suele presentar una complejidad particular para el análisis. La proximidad y la presencia de actores aún en pugna zamarrean al objeto de estudio, lo vuelven opaco. Si a eso le sumamos los condicionamientos de época, la cosa se dificulta más. Salas, en lugar de esconder su perplejidad, la pone en evidencia; la contrasta con información, con notas, con fuentes, con opiniones, con ideas. Y entonces el libro, en su zona de riesgo, es justo donde despliega su mayor fuerza. Allí es donde se convierte en tribuna de debate, en puerta abierta a la acción: un espacio donde la contienda y la disputa respiran, discuten, están vivas.


El movimiento piquetero es una organización de base que nace de tensiones histórico políticas, de altísimos niveles de desigualdad, de una asimetría insoportable entre quienes deciden el destino de miles que viven bajo leyes que los ahorcan, sin gozar nunca de las garantías que debieran protegerles.


Actualmente, la ofensiva ultraderechista del Ejecutivo ha escalado todas las formas posibles del agravio contra los movimientos piqueteros. Pero como su despotismo es directamente proporcional a su falta de imaginación, a pesar del oneroso costo que implica erigir un cerco informativo que se pretende impenetrable; y saturar de mentiras los canales oficiales y extraoficiales para criminalizar toda clase de protesta, no ha podido desactivar estas bases.


Ante la insistencia de un orden único posible, la memoria y presencia de una organización que confronta el orden establecido por las clases dominantes es clave para futuros menos sombríos. Quizá por eso la historización y análisis de estas luchas sea fundamental para comprender y, sobre todo, elegir una orientación singular para la acción directa. Las clases dominantes sostienen el statu quo hasta el momento en que entienden que hay que modificarlo para perpetuar las injusticias, o radicalizarlas.


Cacerolazo contra el gobierno de De la Rúa. 19 de diciembre de 2001


En una nueva entrega, la exhaustiva investigación de

Nicolás Salas

, publicada por

ANRed,


Legüero

y

La Caldera

, reconstruye sin concesiones el modo en que el kirchnerismo neutralizó parte de la fuerza que las organizaciones sociales supieron tener durante su nacimiento y emergencia en contextos de contracción de la economía y reducción del gasto público (fin del menemato, De La Rua, Duhalde) y recupera discusiones fundamentales para una actualidad política que pretende someter al conjunto de la población y al territorio …

author: Rizomatica
title: Cuatro nuevas solicitudes ECMPO son rechazadas en Los Lagos
content:
Los rechazos se suman a una oleada de decisiones sin fundamentos técnicos que condiciona la aprobación de nuevos ECMPO a que se modifique la Ley Lafkenche.


Por: Constanza Ulloa Millaguir, Observatorio Ciudadano


La Comisión Regional de Uso del Borde Costero (CRUBC) de Los Lagos rechazó cuatro solicitudes de Espacios Costeros Marinos de Pueblos Originarios (ECMPO) que llevaban entre 7 y 10 años en trámite y modificaciones. Con éstos, ya son 18 peticiones rechazadas desde 2024, casi el 100% a excepción de uno en la región de La Araucanía. Las comunidades solicitantes y organizaciones de la sociedad civil denuncian que la decisión carece de fundamentos técnicos y se suma a una oleada de rechazos que, en los hechos, condiciona la aprobación de nuevos ECMPO a que se modifique la Ley Lafkenche (20.249), y que sería ilegal.


Yohana Coñuecar

, dirigenta Mapuche Williche e integrante de la CRUBC Los Lagos en representación de los escaños de pueblos originarios, afirmó:


«Hay una ideología en el rechazo de las solicitudes de espacios costeros, más allá de elementos técnicos (…) Hoy día las comisiones regionales ya no son solo una institución o un espacio técnico-político: es un espacio político. Por lo tanto, acá sí hay un lineamiento político de rechazar los espacios costeros, a pesar de que se presenten argumentos, se presenten acuerdos, se presente mucho trabajo anterior. Ya no tiene sentido venir a estos lugares a discutir nuestros derechos, porque finalmente la comisión, en un acto político, decide rechazar.»


YOHANA COÑUECAR – DIRIGENTE MAPUCHE WILLICHE


El mismogobernador regional de Los Lagos,

Alejandro Santana

, sostuvo:


«Nosotros como gobierno regional tenemos una opinión de que es importante hacer una modificación a la Ley Lafkenche. No se puede seguir manteniendo la condición de que estas votaciones sean a favor o en contra de alguien. Aquí lo que tiene que prevalecer es la política de largo plazo, que se tiene que sustentar con la historia reciente: que los ECMPO afectan el territorio en materia de certeza jurídica, de desarrollo, de inversión pública y de empleabilidad. Y eso es lo que ha prevalecido en las votaciones de la CRUBC.»


ALEJANDRO SANTANA GOBERNADOR LOS LAGOS


Alfredo Quintupurray

, presidente de la Comunidad Histórica de Yaldad, una de las cuatro rechazadas, señaló:


«Lamentable que una vez más se rechacen cuatro ECMPO el mismo día. Esto no es más que racismo y clasismo extremo: es coartar la posibilidad de coexistencia de las comunidades que habitan nuestro territorio. Lo único que buscaba el ECMPO Yaldad —que era el ECMPO más completo, donde hubo más acuerdos de negociación— era precisamente el resguardo, el ordenamiento, el cuidado del territorio. Porque hoy día el agua que tomamos, las frutas, la carne y el pescado que comemos salen del territorio.»


ALVARO QUINTUPURRAY -PDTE. COMUNIDAD YALDAD


Las solicitudes rechazadas


Puluqui–Tabón, Calbuco:

 56.000 hectáreas en dos islas, destinadas a resguardar la pesca y recolección de algas tradicionales.


Yaldad, Quellón:

 1.098 hectáreas en un estero con alta presencia de concesiones de mitilicultura y una población relevante de delfín chileno. Contaba con el apoyo del municipio, pescadores artesanales, mitilicultores, la junta de vecinos y organizaciones locales.


Nercón, Castro:

 280 hectáreas asociadas a un humedal urbano, aves migratorias y hábitat de pequeños cetáceos.


Isla Tranqui, Queilen:

 56.962 hectáreas en un territorio con fuerte presencia de actividades salmoneras y mitilicultoras.


Plazos legales incumplidos


La Ley Lafkenche establece un plazo máximo de dos años y medio para resolver una solicitud ECMPO. Las cuatro solicitudes rechazadas llevaban entre 7 y 10 años esperando una decisión y negociando modificaciones. Las comunidades afectadas ya recurrieron a la justicia, acusando que esta demora vulnera sus derechos.


Contexto: presión por modificar la ley


Organizaciones y comunidades vinculadas a los ECMPO advierten que existe una presión activa desde sectores acuícolas y políticos para modificar la Ley Lafkenche, y que autoridades regionales han votado en línea con esa postura, argumentando que los ECMPO frenan la inversión. En paralelo, en el Senado se tramita una reforma a la ley que las comunidades denuncian por no incluir un proceso de Consulta Indígena.


¿Qué es un ECMPO?

title: Trump Has Made Up to $15M in Oil and Gas Stock Rise Spurred in Part by Iran War
content:
Americans have paid an additional $72 billion on gas because of the war, boosting profits and Trump’s portfolio.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

President Donald Trump’s deeply unpopular war on Iran has helped inject millions of dollars into his personal wealth while saddling everyday Americans with a $72 billion bill, a new report reveals.

Amid the war, oil and gas companies’ stocks have skyrocketed in value as companies report staggering earnings; ExxonMobil recently reported its profits doubling year-over-year, while Chevron’s net income has increased nearly 400 percent as a result of the disruptions to the global oil market. In all, oil and gas companies reported $125 billion in profits in the first half of 2026, with a corresponding jump in stock value across the fossil fuel industry.

As a result of that rise, Trump may have profited as much as $15.5 million, and netted at least $4.6 million, from his oil and gas holdings this year, Democrats on Congress’s Joint Economic Committee (JEC) found in a report this week. In all, his oil and gas holdings went from a maximum value of $45.5 million to as much as $61 million.

The analysis was based on stocks that Trump held at the end of 2025, including Exxon, Chevron, and seven other oil and gas companies. His profits may be even higher than the report suggests, as Trump bought additional oil and gas stocks in the first three months of 2026 worth up to $3.6 million. These were bought in a period when the U.S. seized control of Venezuela’s oil profits and launched a war on Iran that has sent oil prices sky-high.

Meanwhile, the rise in energy prices has cost Americans an additional $71.5 billion in gas prices at the pump, the Democrats found, or an average of over $600 a household. That’s before taking into account the hike in prices for things like groceries and other associated costs like increased mortgage rates caused by the war.

“President Trump continues to get richer from an illegal war that he started and refuses to resolve, while Americans pay the price for his actions,” said Sen. Maggie Hassan, the committee’s top Democrat.

Trump’s direct profits from his war on Iran add to a growing list of ways that the president has boosted his personal wealth during his time back in office.

Earlier this month, the JEC Democrats released a separate report finding that Trump reported $2.2 billion in income in 2025 — while families have had to spend an additional $3,500 on average in the first year and a half of Trump’s second presidency due to inflated prices.

Trump’s stock portfolio has come under particular scrutiny as he’s made thousands of trades involving companies who are directly affected by his policies — sparking insider trading concerns as well as alarm over the fact that he owns individual stocks to begin with, which is already extremely unusual for a president.

Recent disclosures showed that Trump made more than 1,000 transactions in June alone, involving purchases of at least $49 million in stocks and sales of at least $28.5 million. The White House claims that he is not personally involved in managing his portfolio, and “there are no conflicts of interest” in his stock activity.

On Monday, Trump said that Exxon and Chevron are “making too much money” and said the companies are raising their prices amid the war. Gas prices have soared to over $4 a gallon on average across the country, spurring further public opposition to the unpopular, expensive war.

author: Ian Karbal
title: Pennsylvania Reports US’s First Confirmed Measles-Related Deaths This Year
content:
The Trump administration has come under scrutiny for spreading misinformation and fear around vaccines.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

The Pennsylvania Department of Health confirmed two measles-related deaths in Lancaster County. Both people, who lived in the county, were unvaccinated. No other personal details were provided in order to protect their families’ privacy.

They are the first confirmed measles-related deaths in the nation this year, and come amid the country’s largest outbreak of measles in decades.

“My deepest sympathies are with the loved ones who are facing this unimaginable loss,” said Pennsylvania Health Secretary Dr. Debra Bogen. “Because measles was largely eliminated in the Commonwealth for more than three decades, people are not familiar with this disease and don’t fully understand the potential severity of the illness. We want to ensure every Pennsylvanian has the information they need to protect themselves, their loved ones and their communities. As a physician, I want to make sure that people understand that the MMR vaccine is safe and provides the best protection we have against measles.”

The United States declared measles eliminated in 2000, due to the success of a widespread vaccination campaign. But the country’s measles-free status is now at risk, with 2,777 cases confirmed by the Centers for Disease Control this year so far.

That’s more than all of last year, which saw 2,289 cases and three deaths. Until this year, it was the highest known annual case count in more than three decades

Pennsylvania has so far reported 393 cases in 29 counties in 2026. Eighty-six cases were reported in the last week, and 70 have resulted in hospitalization. Nearly half of them this year have been in Lancaster County.

Measles is a highly contagious disease that spreads through infected people breathing, coughing or sneezing. Individuals with measles develop high fevers, coughs and red, watery eyes. That’s followed by a characteristic rash three to five days after symptoms begin. 20% of cases end with hospitalization.

Following the announcement of the two deaths, Gov. Josh Shapiro said the state will continue to host pop-up vaccination clinics in affected areas. This past July, 35,000 Pennsylvanians received vaccinations. For context, that’s 10,000 more than typical.

“As a father of four children, I know every parent wants what’s best for their kids – but right now, there’s a barrage of information thrown at us online, on TV, and in our daily lives,” he said. “ I want every Pennsylvanian to know this: measles does not care about your county, your faith, or your social circle. It’s vital for every parent to know that if you or your kids are unvaccinated, you are at an increased risk for contracting this highly-contagious virus.”

The Trump administration has come under scrutiny for spreading misinformation and fear around vaccines.

Weeks ago, President Donald Trump signed an executive order calling for the MMR (measles, mumps, rubella) vaccine to be split into three separate shots. At a press conference announcing the order, he claimed the combined vaccination could be “lethal,” despite no evidence.

The Centers for Medicaid Services administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz, a former Pennsylvania U.S. Senate candidate, later refuted Trump’s claim.

Medical professionals say the shot is safe and effective as is, and warn splitting it into three has no safety benefits and will only make it more likely for people to miss doses.

U.S. Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy also has a long history of casting doubt on the effectiveness of vaccines generally, and making unfounded claims linking jabs to autism and exaggerating the potential for harm.

Before helming the U.S. Health Department, he was the chair of an anti-vaccine nonprofit called the Children’s Health Defense. In that role, he advocated for alternative treatments for vaccine-curable diseases and spread misinformation about vaccine safety.

He has also left his mark on U.S. vaccine policy. Last year, he replaced a 17-person vaccine advisory council at the CDC. He has also hired vaccine skeptics at the Department of Health and Human Services as the department cut funding to vaccine research.

author: dialogocomospovos
title: Memória, arte e inovação no 11º Encontro de Mulheres Negras e Quilombolas
content:
No 11º encontro de mulheres negras e quilombolas, realizado no Engenho da Ponte em Cachoeira, a artista Nath Herrera realizou uma intervenção artística que uniu passado e presente em uma homenagem emocionante.


Sua obra foi dedicada a Dona Dulce, uma grande matriarca do território que recentemente se encantou. Ao retratá-la, Nath destacou que aquela mulher foi uma ancestral guardiã do território. Para a artista, representar Dona Dulce foi uma honra, pois ela permanece como força e símbolo de resistência no lugar.


O que tornou a homenagem ainda mais especial foi a fusão entre tecnologia moderna e ancestralidade. Nath utilizou óculos de realidade aumentada para criar o esboço da obra, unindo inovação à tradição. Ela contou que fez todo o esboço com o auxílio da tecnologia e depois foi preenchendo o grafite, que foi realizado durante o evento, permitindo que os presentes acompanhassem todo o processo criativo.


A emoção tomou conta do momento, especialmente quando os filhos e netos de Dona Dulce presenciaram a homenagem. Nath relatou que eles estiveram presentes na pintura e ficaram emocionados ao ver uma pessoa tão importante em suas vidas sendo representada através da arte.


Representante do Recôncavo Baiano, a artista reforçou seu compromisso com o empoderamento feminino por meio do projeto Grafite Delas, que oferece oficinas exclusivas para mulheres. Ela concluiu sua fala incentivando outras mulheres a ocuparem o espaço da arte urbana, afirmando que todos os espaços também pertencem a elas.

author: José Cícero
title: O samba do Tio Esperança
content:
Na manhã de 29 de julho, toda a comunidade do samba e do futebol de várzea se deparou com a Prefeitura de São Paulo demolindo a sede do Grêmio Esportivo Recreativo Cruz da Esperança, na Zona Norte da capital. A ação foi em cumprimento de uma

ordem judicial de reintegração de posse na área

, onde está prevista a construção do Parque Campo de Marte.


Criado em 1958 por um grupo de taxistas negros, o clube ocupava o terreno no Campo de Marte desde o fim da década de 1970. O espaço se tornou referência no futebol de várzea após receber diversos jogadores que foram destaque em times tradicionais: “Todo jogador de bola vinha jogar no Cruz: Basílio, Serginho Chulapa, Solito, Mauro, Casagrande, Viola, Ataliba. Vou até parar de citar nomes, porque corro o risco de esquecer alguém, mas muita gente passou no Cruz”, conta Antônio Marcos, presidente do Cruz da Esperança, conhecido como Tio Toninho.


Três dias após a demolição do espaço, Toninho concedeu entrevista à

Agência Pública

 em sua casa. Visivelmente abatido, até aquele momento ele não havia saído de casa – ainda estava impactado pelo longo processo de negociação com a Prefeitura até a derrubada das paredes que havia ajudado a construir.


Com diversos álbuns de fotografias à mesa, Toninho se emocionou ao rememorar a sua relação com o futebol de várzea, a chegada ao clube na década de 1960, os bailes black que aconteceram entre os anos 1970 e 1980 e as rodas de samba que se mantêm desde os anos 1990. O espaço, também chamado de “Pequena África Paulista”, é apontado como

patrimônio vivo da memória negra

 e da música popular na Zona Norte da cidade.


Apesar da perda do espaço físico, o samba continua acontecendo todos os finais de semana na região da Casa Verde, próximo à antiga sede. E a história ainda não terminou na Justiça: no dia 20 de agosto, o Tribunal Regional Federal da 3ª Região publicou uma decisão que proíbe a Prefeitura de São Paulo e a concessionária de fazer novas intervenções físicas no solo ou subsolo do terreno, incluindo escavações, terraplenagem, fundações, compactação do terreno e outras atividades de impacto equivalente, até que estudos técnicos sobre possíveis vestígios arqueológicos e bens culturais no local sejam realizados.


Para o Tio Toninho,  a decisão da Justiça é positiva para a comunidade, porém chegou tarde. “A notícia [da decisão] pra nós foi muito ótima, se bem que atrasada porque chegou depois da demolição. Se chegasse antes eles não poderiam mexer”, lamenta.


A decisão recente foi motivada, dentre outros elementos, por uma vistoria feita pelo o Instituto do Patrimônio Histórico e Artístico Nacional (Iphan) no local em 18 de junho deste ano. O relatório de fiscalização constatou que a área “apresenta potencial arqueológico relevante”. O documento solicitou ao órgão o aprofundamento dos estudos técnicos antes da realização de novas intervenções por parte da concessionária. A vistoria aconteceu antes da demolição da sede do Cruz da Esperança.

title: Sancar: "İmralı’da Öcalan ve Kandil heyeti görüşmesi olmadı; yayılan notlar gerçek değil"
content:
DEM Parti İmralı Heyeti üyesi Mithat Sancar, eski Diyarbakır Büyükşehir Belediye Başkanı Gültan Kışanak ve İmralı Sekretaryası üyesi Çetin Arkaş, Ankara’da gazetecilerle bir araya gelerek silahsızlanma süreci, 7595 sayılı yasa ve İmralı görüşmelerine ilişkin soruları yanıtladı.
