, haberine göre buluşma yaklaşık iki buçuk saat sürdü. T24 yazarı Gökçer Tahincioğlu ve ANKA ajansı da toplantıyı soru ve yanıtlarıyla aktardılar. 


Sancar: Böyle bir görüşme olmadı


DEM Parti Urfa Milletvekili ve İmraluı Hayati üyesi Prof. Mithat Sancar, Abdullah Öcalan ile PKK yöneticileri arasında İmralı’da yapıldığı iddiasıyla son haftalarda çeşitli mecralarda yayımlanan görüşme notlarının dayandırıldığı görüşmenin gerçek olmadığını söyledi:


Sancar, görüşmenin Öcalan ve PKK adına yapılan açıklamalarla ve devlet yetkililerince de yalanlandığını hatırlattı. 


Solfasol'un haberine göre, Sancar bununla birlikte görüşme ile iletişim arasında bir ayrım yaptı. Öcalan ve Kandil yöneticileri arasında iddia edildiği biçimde bir görüşme olmadığını, ancak ihtiyaç duyulduğunda Öcalan’ın mesajlarının muhataplarına ulaştırıldığını söyledi. Halep kuşatması sırasında ve daha önceki bazı aşamalarda doğrudan mesajların iletildiğini belirten Sancar, ileride başka tür görüşmelerin de yapılmasının mümkün olduğunu söyledi. 


“Mutlak şeffaflık hiçbir süreçte olmadı”


Sancar, gerçek İmralı görüşmelerinin tüm içeriğinin kamuoyuna açıklanmasının ise sürecin işleyişiyle bağdaşmayacağını söyledi. Görüşmelerin bazen üç, bazen beş saat sürdüğünü belirten Sancar, her konuşulanın açıklanamayacağını, dünyadaki benzer süreçlerde de “mutlak şeffaflık” bulunmadığını söyledi.


Sancar ayrıca Öcalan’ın kamuoyuyla doğrudan temas kurabilmesinin yolunun açılmasını istedi. Gazeteciler, akademisyenler, siyasetçiler ve sivil toplum temsilcilerinin Öcalan’la görüşebilmesini savundu; ancak gazetecilerin İmralı’ya gitmesine ilişkin şu anda somut bir plan bulunmadığını belirtti. 


Öcalan’ın İmralı’daki yeri değişmedi


Sancar, Öcalan’ın İmralı’da yeni bir yerleşkeye taşındığı yönündeki haberleri de doğrulamadı. Heyetin Öcalan’la öncekinden daha geniş bir salonda görüştüğünü, ancak kaldığı yerin değişmediğini söyledi:


“Biz görüşmelerimizi evet farklı, daha geniş bir salonda yapıyoruz ama Sayın Öcalan eski yerinde kalmaya devam ediyor.”


Bu bilgi hem Solfasol hem T24'ün toplantı kayıtlarında yer aldı. Sancar, sürecin ilerleyen aşamalarında Öcalan’ın çalışma koşullarının değiştirilmesinin, yeni bir sekretarya veya çalışma arkadaşlarının görevlendirilmesinin gündeme gelebileceğini de belirtti. 


Yeni çağrı yok, Öcalan’ın görevi de henüz kesinleşmedi


Sancar, Öcalan’ın yeni bir silah bırakma çağrısı yapacağı yönündeki haberleri de doğrulamadı. Son İmralı görüşmesinde böyle bir karar alınmadığını, ilerleyen aşamalarda ihtiyaç doğması halinde konunun yeniden değerlendirilebileceğini söyledi. ANKA da Sancar'ın açıklamalarına ilişkin haberinde bu bilgiye yer verdi. 


Sancar’ın verdiği bir başka önemli bilgi, Öcalan’ın Silahsızlanma ve Stratejik Koordinasyon Alt Kurulu’nda görev almasının henüz kararlaştırılmamış olması. Sancar, DEM Parti İmralı Heyeti'nin beklentisinin Öcalan’ın süreçte “etkili, aktif ve tanımlanmış” bir rol üstlenmesi olduğunu, ancak kararı Takip ve Değerlendirme Kurulu’nun vereceğini söyledi. 


Bu açıklama, Pervin Buldan’ın daha önce Öcalan’ın alt kurullarda görev alacağı yönündeki sözlerine de açıklık getiriyor: Heyetin beklentisi bu yönde, ancak 26 Ağustos itibarıyla verilmiş ve ilan edilmiş bir görev kararı yok. 


Silah bırakma planının ayrıntıları heyette yok


Sancar, silahların hangi takvim ve yöntemle tamamen bırakılacağı konusunda heyetin elinde ayrıntılı bilgi bulunmadığını da söyledi. Devlet ile örgüt arasında doğrudan veya Öcalan üzerinden temasların bulunabileceğini belirten Sancar, çalışmaların sürdüğünü ancak ayrıntılarının kendilerinde olmadığını bildirdi. Kısa süre içinde hem devlet hem örgüt tarafından resmî açıklamalar yapılmasını beklediğini söyledi. 


Yasanın ceza ve infaz hükümlerinin uygulanabilmesi için de silahsızlanmaya ilişkin teyit ve tespit kararının beklendiğini belirten Sancar, kararın ardından uygulama aşamasına geçileceğini söyledi. 


Demirtaş yasa kapsamında


Mithat Sancar, Selahattin Demirtaş’ın 7595 sayılı yasadan yararlanıp yararlanamayacağı tartışmasına da açık yanıt verdi:


“Bu yasa net bir şekilde Demirtaş’ı kapsıyor.”

title: US Declares Palestine Action “Terrorist” Group in Latest McCarthyist Crackdown
content:
The “clear goal” of the move is “targeting a few to silence the many,” said UN human rights expert Francesca Albanese.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

The Trump administration announced that it is designating U.K.-based Palestine Action and two other left wing groups as global “terrorist” groups on Wednesday, escalating its McCarthyist crackdown against the left and the Palestine solidarity movement.

The administration is placing sanctions on Palestine Action, a direct action group that has worked to disrupt the pipeline of arms shipments to Israel amid the Gaza genocide. Trump has also targeted Italian tech collective Autistici/Inventati, which the State Department claims has ties to U.S. activists, and Masar Badil, an international group that works toward Palestinian liberation.

The sanctions are being issued under an executive order signed by President George W. Bush, which declared a national emergency to give the government the ability to target terrorist groups shortly after the attacks of September 11, 2001.

The sanctions freeze the assets of the groups in the U.S., including bank accounts, as well as prohibit individuals and institutions in the U.S. from doing business with them. International officials who have faced similar financial sanctions have described being completely unable to access any financial goods and services because of the U.S.’s heavy influence on the global banking and finance systems.

The Treasury Department described the sanctions against Palestine Action as a “complement” to the U.K.’s ban on the group in 2025 under Labour Prime Minister Keir Starmer. Human rights groups, including the UN, warned at the time that the U.K.’s designation of the group as a “terrorist” entity was an extremist act meant to chill dissent. The U.K.’s proscription is still being reviewed by the country’s Supreme Court under an appeal by the group’s co-founder, Huda Ammouri.

“By banning a direct action protest group under terrorism legislation for the first time in British history, Keir Starmer’s government has created a blueprint for authoritarian governments around the world to suppress political dissent, and to criminalise British citizens who travel or live abroad,” said Ammouri, per The Guardian.

The Trump administration’s action is the newest assault in an all-of-government campaign to silence, dismantle, debank, and criminalize left-wing dissenters, as part of the fascist National Security Presidential Memorandum-7 (NSPM-7) and anti-“political terrorism” initiatives that administration officials have accelerated in recent months. The administration has pledged to dismantle all left-wing groups under a wide-ranging definition of “criminal” speech that includes such broad categories as “anti-Americanism” and “anti-capitalism.”

“Far-left extremists, their fronts, and their enablers should be on notice: We will bring the full weight of our economic tools to bear,” said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent in a statement. “Political terrorism has no place in our society, and we will continue to cut the financial lifelines of these groups until they are eliminated.”

There is not a formal mechanism to designate groups as “domestic terrorist organizations,” but the administration has been targeting international groups as a seeming work-around.

Indeed, the State Department claimed that Portland, Oregon-based anti-fascist group Rose City Antifa has ties to the Autistici/Inventati collective, supposedly using the group’s tools to “disseminate doxing lists and release illegally obtained personal information of Federal Immigration and Customs Enforcement.”

Advocates for Palestinian rights decried the designations, saying that they are the latest attempt by the administration to silence anyone opposed to Israel’s genocide in Gaza.

The “clear goal” of the move is “targeting a few to silence the many,” said UN Special Rapporteur on Palestine Francesca Albanese.

“They’re desperately trying to destroy every effective movement against genocide to protect Israel,” said Palestinian journalist Abubaker Abed. “There’s no democracy in the West.”

author: Daron Letts
title: Child medevaced after dog attack in Iqaluit
content:
The City of Iqaluit is investigating a dog attack Monday that left an 11-year-old girl with serious injuries to her head and face.


Mia Joy Nowdlak-Fraser encountered the dog as she was walking between houses in the downtown core of the city, said her mother Kelly Nowdlak.


After receiving care in Iqaluit, Nowdlak and her daughter were medevaced to Ottawa shortly after 8 p.m. Tuesday.


“She needs to be assessed and treated by a plastic surgeon for injuries to her eyelid and for an area where skin is missing,” Nowdlak said through Facebook Messenger, as the pair boarded their flight.

“The specialist will determine the reconstructive treatment required, including skin grafting and repair of the eyelid.”


The dog was at the back of the house at the time of the attack, Nowdlak said.


Nowdlak has made posts on social media about the incident, which have been shared across Nunavut with sentiments of concern about dog control and public safety.


“My biggest concern is making sure what happened to my daughter is taken seriously and that another person or child is not injured,” Nowdlak said.


The City of Iqaluit released a public service announcement Tuesday about the incident, saying the city recognizes the “serious concern” within the community following the attack.


Dog owners are responsible for making sure their their pets do not kill or injure others, or damage property, according to the City of Iqaluit’s animal control bylaw. Whether or not they have care and control of the dog, owners are “guilty of an offence” if the dog “attacks, threatens or injures any person.”


Deputy Mayor Kimberly Smith commented on the incident during Tuesday’s city council meeting, saying RCMP have been in touch with the family.


At first, RCMP took over as the lead investigator, with municipal enforcement providing support.


Nunatsiaq News has reached out to RCMP to ask why they took over the investigation but did not received a response to this question.


Instead, RCMP spokesperson Cpl. Ashley Daley said officers have identified the dog and its owner.


On Wednesday afternoon, city spokesperson Geoff Byrne said in a press release that the investigation had been transferred back to the city because it does not involve criminal activity.


“Based on the information gathered during [the RCMP’s] investigation, the dog was not at large at the time of the incident and was reportedly tethered,” Byrne wrote.


The RCMP has yet to transfer its file to the city’s Municipal Enforcement Department. Once the department’s review is complete, the city will provide an update, he said.


“The City recognizes the seriousness of this incident and the concern it has caused,” Byrne said.


So far this year municipal enforcement has responded to 17 dog bite incidents and seven animal cruelty complaints. The city has put down nine dogs.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: In First, Starbucks Workers United and Its 12,000 Members Call for Boycott
content:
“[I]t is no longer possible to be both a Starbucks customer and in support of workers,” the union said.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

In a first, Starbucks Workers United and its 12,000 members are calling for a boycott of the coffee chain, after spending nearly 5 years pressuring the company to negotiate a first contract since the first location unionized in 2021.

“At a time when working-class people across the country are struggling in a challenging economy, it is no longer possible to be both a Starbucks customer and in support of workers,” the union said in a statement announcing the boycott. “[C]hoosing to spend money at Starbucks is choosing a law breaking corporation over the baristas who make your coffee everyday exactly as you ask for it.”

The union points to determinations that Starbucks has committed hundreds of violations of federal labor law, “more than any other company in modern history,” the group said.

The call for a boycott is an escalation of the union’s fight for a contract with the company. Starbucks workers have previously launched targeted strikes in hopes of forcing the company to the bargaining table.

But the company has refused to agree to a contract with reasonable pay and working conditions, the union has said. This is despite the fact that more than 700 Starbucks locations have unionized since 2021, now representing roughly 5 percent of the company’s workforce.

The goal of the boycott is to achieve a first contract with “a minimum $17/hr wage, enough hours to live on, better staffing in our stores, and basic workplace protection,” as well as an end to Starbucks’s union busting. This is a revised proposal from the union’s previous demand for a $20 an hour minimum wage, which it revised earlier this year in hopes of restarting long-stalled contract negotiations.

“Instead of finalizing a fair and reasonable union contract, Starbucks has repeatedly demonstrated a lack of care for the workers who fuel the company’s profits by wasting millions of dollars on Al and technology that doesn’t work, launching countless gimmicky drinks designed to distract from real problems, and inventing pointless policies that do nothing but make our jobs harder,” the union said.

In response to the boycott, the company said that it’s “committed to engaging in productive bargaining,” and already has “competitive pay” and “industry-leading benefits,” per HuffPost. “People love working at Starbucks which is why we have the lowest turnover in the industry and why more than 1 million people every year apply to wear the green apron,” a company spokesperson said.

The boycott is being backed by the AFL-CIO and the Service Employees International Union (SEIU).

“America’s unions are proud to endorse [Starbucks Workers United]’s boycott of stand-alone corporate Starbucks stores. Workers are fed up with unchecked corporate greed, and we’re standing with them in their fight for a fair contract,” the AFL-CIO said in a statement.

In place of Starbucks, the union published a list of coffee shops that have a collective bargaining agreement that it encouraged supporters to visit instead in locations across the U.S.

The Starbucks union wave helped launch a historic unionization effort of service workers across the U.S. in the early 2020s — but even as some efforts at retail stores like Barnes & Noble and Apple succeeded in gaining a bargaining agreement, other companies like Trader Joe’s and REI still have yet to negotiate a first contract.

author: Hayley Tsukayama
title: EFF's Policy Position on ALPR Surveillance: Eliminate It and Reduce Its Harms
content:
Automated license plate readers (ALPRs) build a searchable map of everywhere a driver goes, fed into databases that police, ICE, and private vendors can query after the fact. Networked across a city, ALPRs are purpose-built to track everyone regardless of suspicion. ALPRs are not a surveillance tool that can be made safe with the right policy or feature update—they are irredeemably harmful.


EFF's position is that ALPR mass surveillance—the indiscriminate, continuous collection and retention of location data on every driver, regardless of suspicion—should not exist. Because it nonetheless does, EFF also urges courts and state legislatures to impose strict, enforceable restrictions, such as warrant requirements and deletion deadlines.


EFF's position is that ALPR mass surveillance—the indiscriminate, continuous collection and retention of location data on every driver, regardless of suspicion—should not exist. Because it nonetheless does, EFF also urges courts and state legislatures to impose strict, enforceable restrictions, such as warrant requirements and deletion deadlines. EFF applies every tool available to eliminate ALPR surveillance and the harm it enacts.


The Case Against ALPRs


A note about scope: This post addresses ALPR mass surveillance. It does not address the wider universe of automated traffic enforcement (ATE) such as conventional red light and speed cameras that solely ticket a specific violation, without retaining or networking data on uninvolved drivers. But lawmakers and purchasers should guard against efforts by vendors to piggyback on ATE contracts to market ALPR mass surveillance systems.


ALPRs are frequently marketed as a narrow tool for specific purposes, such as recovering stolen vehicles. But in practice, these sensors sweep up data on every driver who passes a camera, and store it in searchable databases. That indiscriminate collection and retention is precisely why ALPR-fed surveillance systems can be easily weaponized against immigrants, political dissidents, and other targeted communities as ICE and other federal agencies escalate their assault on civil liberties. There is no configuration of an ALPR network that eliminates this risk, because the risk is the mass surveillance itself, not a misuse of it.


Of course, ALPRs cause other predictable harms. Innocent drivers are recurringly

arrested and menaced

 by police because of ALPR errors. Officers regularly abuse ALPR systems to

stalk

 past and potential romantic partners. Creating any database of personal information—including ALPR surveillance databases—inherently creates

risk of data theft

 and subsequent harm to data subjects. And ALPR

surveillance of protests

 and targeting of activists chill participation in First Amendment-protected dissent. But even if these downstream harms could all be prevented (and they likely can’t), ALPRs would remain an intolerable form of mass surveillance.


Fighting on Every Front to Eliminate ALPR Surveillance


At the city level, EFF works with community members and decision makers to

outright refuse ALPR purchasing

. ALPRs are not inevitable. The same

decision mechanisms

 used to facilitate runaway surveillance purchasing in U.S. localities can be turned against these systems to dismantle them.


EFF also pushes state legislatures to establish

strict state-level limits

 on ALPR surveillance, such as data-deletion rules and use restrictions. Building such constraints into statute can mitigate the harms of existing ALPR systems.


In courts across the country, EFF files amicus briefs arguing that warrantless police searches of ALPR databases

violate the Fourth Amendment

. In California state court, EFF and the ACLU of Northern California are suing on behalf of two community groups, SIREN and CAIR-CA, arguing that the San Jose Police Department's practice of letting officers search stored plate data—to the tune of over 100,000 times a year—without a warrant

violates the California Constitution

. We’ve also sued to block California law enforcement from

sharing ALPR data

 with federal and out-of-state agencies, in violation of a

California statute

.


A big part of EFF’s work is exposing the

harms

 of ALPR surveillance. Our investigative team tirelessly

collects

 information about how law enforcement uses ALPRs with public records requests,

sues

 to enforce such requests, and

publishes reports

 about them. We’ve also successfully lobbied for a

content:

Progressive and pro-Palestine critics on Tuesday accused House Democratic leaders of ignoring the majority of party voters who oppose U.S. military aid to Israel by appointing one of the most pro-Israel members of Congress as the top Democrat on a key Mideast subcommittee.

Rep. Gregory Meeks (D-NY), the leading Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, announced the appointment of Rep. Jared Moskowitz (D-Fla.) as ranking member of the Middle East and North Africa Subcommittee. Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D-Fla.) was assigned to the Oversight and Intelligence Subcommittee, Mark Pocan (D-Wis.) joined the Africa Subcommittee, and Wesley Bell (D-Mo.) was named to the Western Hemisphere Subcommittee.

Moskowitz thanked Meeks and House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY) on social media “for this important responsibility” and, in a separate post, vowed to “work to strengthen America’s relationships with Israel and our Gulf allies, expand regional peace, advance American diplomacy, and ensure our foreign policy is grounded in strength, security, and reality.”

During his two terms in Congress, Moskowitz — who last week survived a primary challenge by pro-Palestine progressive Oliver Larkin — has repeatedly argued against conditioning armed aid to apartheid Israel on compliance with international law or protection of Palestinian civilians amid the ongoing genocide in Gaza and Israel’s illegal occupation, colonization, and ethnic cleansing in the West Bank.

Moskowitz was one of only 12 Democrats who voted for a 2023 Republican aid package to Israel — which receives billions of dollars in annual U.S. funding — as the Israeli military killed thousands of Palestinian civilians in Gaza following the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attack.

Critics argued that placing one of Congress’ most outspoken supporters of Israel in a key Middle East policy position shows that Democratic leadership remains badly out of step with its own voters, a majority of whom concur with a United Nations commission of inquiry, human rights groups, scholars, and around 20 national governments who say Israel is committing genocide in Gaza.

Moskowitz denies the Gaza genocide, has conflated criticism of Israeli crimes with hatred of Jews, and was denounced by House progressives including Rep. Rashida Tlaib (D-Mich.), the only Palestinian American in Congress, for authoring an amendment to ban US officials from using State Department funds to cite official Gaza casualty figures — which now include more than 250,000 Palestinians killed, wounded, or missing during Israel’s onslaught.

Meeks’ appointments come at a time when 3 in 4 Democratic voters oppose U.S. aid to Israel — up from just 45% three years ago — and after the issue was a factor in former Vice President Kamala Harris’ defeat by President Donald Trump in the 2024 presidential election.

In response to Moskowitz’s appointment, the progressive organizing group Demand Progress issued a statement noting that the congressman “has consistently opposed placing conditions on military aid to Israel, repeatedly voted against the majority of House Democrats to sanction International Criminal Court officials, and earlier this year said he would oppose an Iran war powers resolution.”

Demand Progress senior policy adviser Cavan Kharrazian said:

By making a hard-line Israel supporter their point person on Middle East policy, House Democratic leaders are doubling down on a failed approach to Israel that shows contempt for the clear and growing majority of Democratic voters who want to stop cutting blank checks for the Israeli government. Donald Trump’s ongoing wars in the Middle East and his commitment to keeping the U.S. joined at the hip to Israel are wildly unpopular and have been a disaster for the nation. Elevating someone who consistently sides with Trump in support of Israel, and who has a long record as an Iran hawk, represents clear political malpractice on behalf of House Democratic leaders.

title: Trump Is Once Again Weaponing the Postal Service to Try to Undermine Mail Voting
content:
Millions could be disenfranchised with less than 70 days left before the midterms, says journalist Ari Berman.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

The Supreme Court on Monday lifted a lower court’s injunction on President Trump’s executive order seeking to limit mail-in voting ahead of November’s midterm elections. Trump’s order directs the Department of Homeland Security to create state-by-state lists of eligible voters who are citizens. The U.S. Postal Service would then use the lists provided by states to assess whether voters should be allowed to vote by mail. Justices ruled 6 to 3 that California and 22 other states lacked standing to sue over the issue. The ruling, however, did not address whether Trump had authority to impose the rules. A separate nationwide injunction against parts of the same order remains in place.

“This leads to a lot of uncertainty going into the midterms, because the Trump executive order would radically restrict vote by mail,” says Ari Berman, the national voting rights correspondent for Mother Jones. If the ruling goes into effect, “it could disenfranchise millions of voters in November.”

“If voting proceeds based on these DHS lists,” adds Berman, “it’s going to be inaccurate, it’s going to be unconstitutional, and a lot of legitimate American voters are going to be wrongly labeled as noncitizens and unable to vote — either based on shoddy data or an intentional attempt by the Trump administration to prevent people from voting.”

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

NERMEEN SHAIKH: This is Democracy Now!, democracynow.org, The War and Peace Report. I’m Nermeen Shaikh.

With the midterm elections less than 10 weeks away, the Supreme Court has lifted a lower court injunction on President Trump’s executive order seeking to limit mail-in voting ahead of the midterms. Trump’s order directed the Department of Homeland Security to create state-by-state lists of eligible voters who are citizens. The U.S. Postal Service would then use the lists provided by states to assess if voters should be allowed to vote by mail. On Monday, justices ruled 6 to 3 that California and 22 other states lacked standing to sue over the issue. The ruling, however, did not address whether Trump had authority to impose the rules.

The court’s three liberal justices dissented. Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson warned that the majority opinion “needlessly injects chaos and uncertainty into the upcoming midterm elections.”

In related news, on Tuesday, a federal judge in Massachusetts found the Trump administration violated a court injunction by finalizing new regulations with the U.S. Postal Service that would overhaul voting by mail nationwide if they’re enforced. While Trump has repeatedly attacked mail-in voting, he continues to vote by mail himself. Voting records in Florida show the president voted by mail in the recent Republican primary. He requested a ballot in late July. The ballot was returned on August 13th.

Well, we’re joined now by Ari Berman, national voting rights correspondent for Mother Jones. His new piece is titled ”SCOTUS Hands Trump a Temporary Win in His Crusade to Restrict Mail Voting.” Berman is author of the book Minority Rule: The Right-Wing Attack on the Will of the People — and the Fight to Resist It.

Welcome back to the program, Ari. If you could just respond to this news, the latest news?

“, sostiene il gruppo.


È però soprattutto quanto sarebbe avvenuto sulla pista di Pisa a sollevare gli interrogativi. Non viene infatti stabilito se il materiale sia stato caricato o scaricato dal C-17. Da qui la richiesta di chiarimenti alle istituzioni. “

Perché armamenti e velivoli militari stranieri vengono movimentati sulle piste pisane

 senza che la cittadinanza riceva alcuna informazione?”, domanda Diritti in Comune.


Il Movimento No Base di Pisa, attivo contro l’industria delle armi sul territorio, denuncia: “il coinvolgimento bellico italiano passa da qui”.

Nell’audio l’appello pubblico del Movimento No Base.

author: Glen Stellmacher
title: Documents Show How Israeli Methods Were Presented to US Police as a Model
content:
The Advanced Security Training Institute’s programs have largely operated outside of public scrutiny.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

At the King David Hotel in Jerusalem in June 2018, Michael Oren spoke from a podium to a gathering of American police officers, firefighters, and emergency managers. Oren, previously named Michael Bornstein, was serving as a member of the Israeli Knesset after renouncing his U.S. citizenship. “We are defending the same civilization, the same values, the same beliefs. We are you, you are us,” Oren told the group, who had made the trip from the Washington, D.C., area.

“We are fighting for the same cause,” Oren said as he and other Americans stood inside a hotel that was the target of a Zionist terrorist bombing in 1946.

The backdrop behind Oren featured the logo of the Advanced Security Training Institute (ASTI). The Brooklyn-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit hosted the event to honor 25 first responders from Washington, D.C., Maryland, and Virginia who were attending an eight-day training in Israel, according to documents obtained by Prism through public records requests.

Training programs ASTI ran in Israel “use the Israeli experience as a laboratory” to teach American police, according to an internal intelligence division memorandum by the Austin Police Department, which sent some of its members to the sessions. A trove of documents Prism reviewed as part of a multi-part investigative series into the nonprofit shows how Israeli methods for law enforcement and intelligence gathering were presented to U.S. police as a model.

ASTI’s Israeli American founder Yisroel Stefansky also once proposed to bring that laboratory directly to a city in Washington state, offering to train local police on how to operate informant networks to surveil Americans based on “proven [Israeli] intelligence doctrine.” The proposal was not implemented.

Stefansky did not respond to numerous requests for an interview or an email detailing Prism’s findings. Oren declined to comment.

While other police training programs run by the Anti-Defamation League, American Israel Public Affairs Committee, the Jewish Institute for National Security in America, and the Georgia International Law Enforcement Exchange have been widely reported, ASTI’s programs have largely operated outside of public scrutiny.

Over two years, Prism submitted dozens of public records requests to agencies across the U.S., aiming to uncover the scope of ASTI training, and received thousands of pages of documents. Prism traced law enforcement training programs as far back as 2005 across Washington state to Colorado, Texas, and Washington, D.C. The documents map out how a series of little-known police training entities, including ASTI, have crossed paths with law enforcement agencies across the country.

This is the third report in Prism’s series “The ASTI Files,” primarily based on these public records.

Prism uncovered documents from ASTI training programs in Israel from as recently as 2019. After Hamas’ Operation Al-Aqsa Flood on Oct. 7, 2023, ASTI proposed training programs in Seattle, Dallas, and San Francisco, according to public records. Seattle and San Francisco police departments told Prism that they did not engage in any training with ASTI. Dallas did not respond to a request for comment.

ASTI is active on X and maintains a website where it advertises its programs. However, the scope of its current partnerships with police across the country is unclear.

Seattle Gay News previously reported that ASTI’s X account regularly liked anti-LGBTQIA+ and anti-immigrant content. Prism’s investigation has also revealed that the organization’s training included materials that advocates and experts interviewed by Prism viewed as anti-Muslim.

ASTI has given lectures to American emergency personnel about topics such as the “Muslim Mindset,” the importance of monitoring social media, specialized surveillance tactics, understanding crowd behavior, and hands-on weapons training. Some of these lectures took place at what Haaretz has called an “anti-terror fantasy camp” named Caliber 3, inside the Israeli-occupied West Bank.

At Caliber 3, learning objectives from older trainings run by another one of Stefansky’s companies, Proactive Global Security (PGS), included “shooting from a moving vehicle,” close quarters battle tactics, and …

author: David Greene
title: EFF Statement on Meta Settlement
content:
Under

this settlement

, young users will now have less access to Meta products, and a lesser ability to exercise their rights to speak, access information and art and culture, associate and form communities, and play. The settlement also embeds age assurance into every product, mandating the collection of even more personal information from users of all ages; this enshrines Meta's harmful surveillance into law, and it will compromise users' privacy and anonymity while increasing their exposure to data breaches and government data requests. And the data minimization and security measures don’t keep states from using data collected under the agreement for other law enforcement purposes – which could include things like criminal investigations of abortions or gender-affirming care.

author: Unknown
title: New lead in Rojin Kabaiş case: Lawyer points to drugs found in autopsy
content:
New questions have emerged regarding the forensic findings in the case of university student Rojin Kabaiş, who was found dead in 2024. The family’s lawyer, Abdurrahman Karabulut, compared records from an operation performed shortly before her disappearance with the autopsy and forensic reports.


Two substances detected in the 21-year-old Rojin’s body have now become a particular focus. According to Karabulut, rocuronium was detected in her stomach and internal organs, while ornidazole was found in her stomach contents. The findings themselves had already been documented in the forensic reports. However, the family’s lawyer is now challenging the previous explanation for the origin of these substances and believes they could potentially indicate that she was killed.


Powerful muscle relaxant detected


Rocuronium is a powerful muscle relaxant used during surgery and in emergency medicine, particularly for intubation. It temporarily blocks the transmission of nerve impulses to the muscles, including the respiratory muscles. Accordingly, the drug is administered under medical supervision.


Ornidazole is a medication used to treat certain bacterial infections and parasites and may also be used in connection with surgical procedures.


Kabaiş underwent surgery on September 11, 2024. She disappeared from the campus of Yüzüncü Yıl University in Van on September 27, and her body was found on the shore of Lake Van on October 15.


Karabulut considers it impossible that the rocuronium detected later could still have been attributable to the surgery performed several weeks earlier. Among other things, he points to the drug’s short half-life and calls for the toxicological findings to be reassessed.


In his view, the findings suggest that Kabaiş may have received the substances shortly before her death. He argues that she was administered ornidazole and, in particular, rocuronium, and that the muscle relaxant may have paralyzed her respiratory muscles.


However, no new forensic assessment confirming this conclusion has yet been issued. Nor can a drug’s half-life alone be used to determine directly how long the substance or its metabolites may remain detectable in toxicological testing under postmortem conditions.


Doubts over previous forensic examinations


The findings concerning the drugs add to a series of existing questions surrounding the Kabaiş case. From the outset, the family and their legal counsel have rejected the suicide theory raised early in the investigation by the authorities and believe the case to be an unresolved suspected femicide.


The previously assumed cause of death is also disputed. The family and their lawyer have long criticized the fact that no diatom test was conducted during the autopsy, a forensic procedure used in cases of suspected drowning. They are therefore calling for a new forensic examination. If the remaining samples are insufficient for such testing, they are also considering exhumation.


Two male DNA traces remain unexplained


Two different male DNA traces found on Kabaiş’s body had already raised significant doubts about the original direction of the investigation. The forensic report also contains findings that raise questions about possible sexual violence. The family and their legal counsel have been particularly critical of the authorities’ handling of these findings.


The lawyer was only granted access to key forensic documents long after the young woman’s death. The family accuses the investigating authorities of failing to pursue crucial evidence consistently and of delaying access to relevant information.


Almost two years after Rojin Kabaiş’s death, key questions therefore remain unanswered. The drug findings now under scrutiny raise yet another: When, how, and under what circumstances did rocuronium and ornidazole enter her body?

author: Nehaa Bimal
title: Umiujaq daycare remains in temporary space as renovations pushed to 2027
content:
Nearly two years after a burst pipe forced Umiujaq’s Amautik Childcare Centre to

close

, children are still attending daycare in a temporary municipal building — and renovations to the original facility have been pushed to the spring.


In an Aug. 19 interview, Amautik director Lizzie Tooktoo said she wasn’t sure what caused the delay but that she heard it could be because Kativik Regional Government, which operates Amautik, was looking for a contractor.


A heating system failure in December 2024 damaged the original building. In November 2025, Amautik found a temporary home at the sports complex while it awaited renovations for the original building.


Repairs were initially expected to begin in fall 2025, after construction materials arrived by sealift, with reopening anticipated this spring or summer, Tooktoo told Nunatsiaq News a year ago.


KRG did not respond to questions from Nunatsiaq News about the renovation. 


Amautik now shares the sports complex — a large, gymnasium-like space — with the village’s recreation department, which takes over after the child-care centre closes at 5 p.m., Tooktoo said.


The space is divided into two areas for the different age groups, and staff continue to offer the same day-to-day supervision and group child care they did at the original centre.


Internet access has been a major issue at the sports complex, however, said Tooktoo, who said she has arranged for Starlink satellite internet service to be installed.


The centre currently has eight staff members who care for 30 children between the ages of six months to just over three years old. P

arents at Amautik pay a subsidized daily rate of $9.65 per child to use the centre’s services.


The renovation plan will largely preserve the building’s existing structure, Tooktoo said. She participated in at least two meetings with KRG officials this year and said a wheelchair ramp is among the planned additions.

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: Nunavut premier looks to reducing internal trade barriers
content:
Nunavut Premier John Main wants to see the territory trade more within Canada, saying the trade war with the U.S. could end up being a “lengthy dispute.”


The U.S. has

imposed

 50 per cent tariffs on close to $30 billion of Canadian goods, including dairy, alcohol and cement. Canada will soon launch counter tariffs that target $27.6 billion worth of American goods in response, to come into effect after Labour Day.


A report released earlier this summer by the Canadian Federation of Independent Businesses gave Nunavut the lowest score in the country when it comes to reducing barriers to internal trade, mainly due to hunting and fishing protections in the territory. 


Main acknowledged that “

we have a lot of work to do” when it comes to reducing barriers to internal trade between the territory and other jurisdictions.


“One of the biggest things we can do to respond to these threats is to make sure we’re building up Canada and that we’re investing in developments in our own country,” the premier said Tuesday at the legislative assembly in Iqaluit.


“We do see a lot of benefit in better trade within Canada.”


There are no specific territorial supports in place yet for Nunavummiut who might be impacted by the trade war, Main said, adding his government is still monitoring potential impacts.


The federal government meanwhile has committed $7.6 billion toward supporting workers and businesses. Much of that money will go toward increasing the duration of Employment Insurance payments and grants businesses can use to retain workers.


Main said he’s been in discussion with leaders in the mining industry about how they might be impacted.


The cost of living in the territory is his primary concern.


“[Nunavut] is already the most expensive place in the country to run a business, to raise a family, to survive in daily life,” Main said Tuesday as he spoke alongside Trade Minister Craig Simailak. 


Simailak said advancing internal trade between the territory and the provinces will be the subject of discussions during the Federal, Provincial and Territorial Committee meeting he’s scheduled to host later this week in Iqaluit. Federal Internal Minister Dominic LeBlanc sits on the committee alongside premiers and ministers from across the country.


“We’re trying to strengthen the One Canadian Economy that our prime minister has been working on,”

Simailak

said about Mark Carney’s commitment to remove internal trade barriers and boost the Canadian economy through prioritizing major infrastructure projects.


“For the most part, all jurisdictions have been putting aside their party politics and seeing what we can do to help make Canada better together, and that’s what I’m expecting this Thursday during the internal trade conference,” he said.

author: Unknown
title: Fate of two Kurdish women unknown two months after arrests in Iran
content:
The fate of Kurdish women Parvin (Akhtar) Rasegh Ghezelbash and Zahra Pir-Dehghan remains unknown two months after their arrests by forces of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Intelligence Organisation in Orumiyeh.


According to the Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN), Pir-Dehghan, 32, from Chaldoran, and Rasegh Ghezelbash, 33, from Maku, were arrested on 25 and 28 June respectively.


They were transferred to the IRGC Intelligence Organisation’s detention facility at the al-Mahdi military base in Orumiyeh.


Over the past two months, their families have repeatedly approached the court, the Ministry of Intelligence and the IRGC Intelligence Organisation in the city, seeking information about their daughters.


However, the security and judicial authorities have continued to refuse to provide any information or explanation about their fate.


The reasons for their arrests and the charges brought against remain unknown.

author: Paige Collings
title: French Top Court Gets It Right, Strikes Down Social Media Ban For Youths
content:
Earlier this month, France’s top court

struck down

 the country’s legislation that

banned social media

 use for people under 15 years old, which had been scheduled to take effect in January 2027. This is a welcome win for free expression, as we face a wave of

countries and U.S. states

 seeking to pass similar laws banning young people from social media. 


In particular, the Constitutional Council’s decision focused on two components:


Infringement on Free Expression


The Council

ruled

 that the legislation banning under-15s from social media infringed on freedom of expression and communication in a manner that is not appropriate, necessary, or proportionate, which is required by Article 34 of the French Constitution. In particular, it stressed that the ban did not distinguish between different types of online services, and ignored the circumstances of individual users, such as their exact age, level of maturity, and family situation.


The

evidence

 is

clear

: these are reckless and harmful laws that negatively impact all people, not just those under 15. These measures chill all users’ exercise of the right to free speech and expression online by imposing obstacles on sites or by wrongfully blocking people’s access outright.


By forcing young people into digital isolation, these bans curtail vital access to

news

 and

resources

 for health and development; especially for

LGBTQ+

 and

marginalized youth

 as social media can often be the only place to find community, explore their identity, or access life-saving resources. They also completely ignore the

calls of young people themselves

 who favor digital literacy and education over surveillance and government control. 


These bans also destroy the

right to online anonymity

—a cornerstone of our right to free expression that in particular protects whistleblowers, journalists, activists, and immigrants.


Infringement on the Right to Private Life 


The Council’s second objection

noted

 that the law requiring every person, even adults, to prove their age before accessing social media platforms impedes the right to private life, and thus infringes on Article 2 of the Déclaration de 1789.


The French Council gets a lot right in this decision: it highlights that bans like this impact not just young people, but everyone online. They force people of all ages to hand over

government IDs

,

face scans

, and

other sensitive information

 into a growing surveillance ecosystem. Further, when parental consent is required, companies must collect

even more

 verification data on the parents.


We know that when people are forced to hand over this information, age verification systems frequently misidentify or lock out

people of color

,

people with disabilities

, and

trans or gender-nonconforming

 individuals whose IDs may not match their appearance; adding to the privacy concerns around these bans.


Next Steps 


As all bills in France are subject to scrutiny by the Constitutional Council to ensure compliance with the French Constitution, French President Emmanuel Macron has tasked Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu to

re-work the legislation

 with a goal to adopt a ‘legally robust’ version of the social media ban. 


Public policy must be effective, proportionate, and respectful of fundamental rights; and the ruling by the Constitutional Council has ramifications beyond France. It sends a message of caution to Brussels, where the EU Commission is

working

 on an EU-wide bill on access restrictions. These legal restrictions would likely require problematic age verification of users. The prominent

EU digital identity wallet

 and the “mini” age verification app, presented as privacy-robust options, instead raise serious

privacy and security concerns

.


Young people deserve better than a policy built on panic, and all internet users deserve a safe and free internet that includes measures to empower all people with the knowledge they need to navigate online spaces safely. A social media ban generates headlines, but it will not solve the problem.

author: Unknown
title: YJA Star commemorates the martyrs: “We pledge to prove ourselves worthy of their memory”
content:
The Free Women’s Troops (YJA Star) commemorated the guerrilla fighters whose deaths could only recently be announced due to the severe conditions of war.


YJA Star Central Headquarters Command extended its condolences to the families and honored the martyrs as the foundation of the decades-long freedom struggle in Kurdistan.


The YJA Star statement on Wednesday reads as follows:


“Our martyrs, who are the source of our life and struggle and the lifeblood of our very existence, constitute the foundation of the Kurdistan Freedom Struggle. Our freedom movement, a movement of martyrs, has built itself upon commitment to the memory of our martyrs and the realization of their goals.


In an age in which meaninglessness is imposed upon us, our martyrs, through the meaning they gave to life, kept alive the struggle to remain human and became the embodiment of the insistence on humanity in the face of the meaninglessness imposed upon peoples and women. It is our martyrs who have carried our freedom struggle from its beginnings to the present day and given our people an honored place among humanity.


From the time when our struggle was only beginning to take root until today, we have advanced alongside our martyrs, and it is our martyrs who have sustained our existence from the very first day of our movement to the present. As women of Kurdistan, our discovery of freedom, our embrace of it, and our journey toward it did not come easily; it was forged through boundless labor, effort, and struggle.


Our martyrs have been a breath of life for every individual, gender, and class engaged in the freedom struggle across Kurdistan, revealing the truth that a free life can only be achieved through great resistance.


The voice of free life and women


In this sense, the resistance of our martyrs has formed the foundation of the Kurdistan revolution and the ethic of freedom that has developed in Kurdistan. In the face of all forms of degradation imposed upon society, they became the voice and action of human dignity, free life, and free women.


The price of rebelling against enslavement and domination on the path to freedom has also been great. In many places and at many times, freedom has redefined itself and acquired meaning through these sacrifices. The history of every people, class, and gender contains countless unique examples of this kind. Our own history of freedom likewise possesses a vast and magnificent legacy of resistance.


The foundations of this legacy have manifested themselves in their most remarkable form over the past decade. In the intense clashes with the Turkish state, we lost many of our people’s most precious sons and daughters as martyrs. Due to the intensity and severity of the war, we were unable to announce the martyrdom of our comrades at the time.


We considered it our duty to announce our martyrs, even if belatedly. For this reason, we now commemorate our comrades who fell at different times and in different regions of Kurdistan.


Condolences to the families


First and foremost, we extend our heartfelt condolences to the valued families of our martyrs who have been commemorated in recent days in Amed (Diyarbakır), Istanbul, Van, Gever (Yüksekova), Cizre and Mardin, as well as to our patriotic people. We commemorate the martyrs of freedom with love and gratitude, bow respectfully before their memory, and renew our pledge to fulfill the goals of freedom for which they gave their lives.


We believe that our martyrs will be embraced and commemorated with great honor in cities throughout Kurdistan and abroad, particularly in the provinces and districts where commemorations have been held. One of our most fundamental duties toward our martyrs is to commemorate them in the manner they deserve and to raise the banners of their struggle high.


Our martyrs are those who followed the path of the Leader’s truth, spread throughout Kurdistan the light created by the reality of the Leader, and laid the foundations for a free life. They paved the way for the construction of a free and democratic life in Kurdistan.


They will always live on and their memory will be kept alive


Now is the time to take up the banner where they left off and realize their dreams by participating actively and creatively in the Initiative for a Democratic Society and Peace, together with the Free Leader, for a Free and Democratic Kurdistan. As long as a free and democratic society succeeds and our people are free, our martyrs will …

title: Spot elektrik piyasasında fiyatlar geriledi
content:
Enerji Piyasaları İşletme AŞ (EPİAŞ) tarafından açıklanan güncel verilere göre, spot elektrik piyasasındaki işlem hacmi bir önceki güne kıyasla %6,5 oranında düşerek 2 milyar 531 milyon 268 bin 585 lira seviyesine geriledi.

Gün öncesi piyasada yarın geçerli olacak elektrik fiyatlarında gün içindeki dalgalanma belirginleşti:

Tavan fiyat: Zirve tüketimin yaşandığı saat 19.00’da megavatsaat başına 4.300 TL ile en yüksek seviyeye ulaşacak.

Taban fiyat: Günün en düşük maliyetli elektriği ise saat 12.00’de megavatsaat başına 2.125,99 TL olarak gerçekleşecek.

Ortalama değerler: Piyasadaki aritmetik ortalama fiyat 3.466,41 TL, ağırlıklı ortalama fiyat ise 3.497,47 TL olarak hesaplandı.

Tablo, yarın için spot elektrik tavan ve taban fiyatlarında düne kıyasla hafif bir düşüş yaşandığını gösteriyor.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Unknown
title: Bavê Rojîn Kabaîşê: Kesên ku dixwazin bûyerê binuximîne derketine holê
content:
Xwendekara zanîngehê Rojîn Kabaîş li Wanê 18 roj piştî ku wenda bû cenazeyê wê hatibû dîtin. Parêzerê malbatê Abdurrahman Karabulut ji bo ku derbarê du kesan de biryara desteserkirinê bê dayîn serî li dozgeriyê da.


Bavê Rojînê, Nizamettin Kabaîş têkildarî mijarê bi bianetê re axivî û got: "Zaroka min di rewşeke wisa de nebû ku xwe bikuje, min ev tişt ji destpêkê ve dizanibû û em ê derfetê nedin wab kesên ku dixwazin vê bûyerê binuxumînin."


"Kesên ku dixwazin binuxumînin hene"


Kabaiş wiha axivî:


"Ez bavek im. Dayik û bav ew in ku zarokên xwe herî baş nas dikin. Zaroka min di rewşeke wisa de nebû ku xwe bikuje, min ev tişt ji destpêkê ve dizanibû û em ê derfetê nedin wab kesên ku dixwazin vê bûyerê binuxumînin. Li cihê bûyerê av tune bû, geriyan û nedîtin, zarok 24 kîlometre dûr hat dîtin. Gava ku hûn van hemûyan bînin cem hev ev bi eşkereyî bûyereke kuştinê ye. Niha dê li cihê ku bûyer çêbûye û li gundê gumanbar ê ku yekser li kêleka zanîngehê ye dê li DNAya 2 hezar û 500 kesî mêzekin. Heta niha lêkolîna DNAya 600 kesî hat kirin lê heta niha tu lihevhatin çênebûye. Kesên ku dixwazin serê bûyerê binuxumînin hene. Kesên ku dixwazin bûyerê binuxumînin derketine holê. Em dixwazin ku rastî vê meselê çî ye bila derkeve holê.”


“Em ê dîsa bi Wezîrê Dadê re hevdîtinê bikin”


Nizamettin Kabaiş bal kişand ser daneyên di raporên otopsî û bijîşkiya dadî yên keça xwe de û bi taybetî li ser hûrgiliya dermanan a di dosyayê de ev agahî dan:


“Em du roj in bi berdewamî difikirin; gelo çi anîn serê vê zarokê? Di mîdeya keça min de du dermanên cuda hatine tespîtkirin. Ew derman ne tiştên wisa ne ku her kes bi hêsanî bikirin, tenê dermanên wisa ne ku bi destûra bijîşkan tên girtin û mirovan hema hema felç dikin û ji hiş dibin. Wate destpêkê derman dane wî û ew ji hiş birine. Min çi di dosyayê de dîtibe li ser televizyonan anî ziman. Heke ez tênekoşiyam, dibeku ev dosye di serî de weke ‘xwekuştin’ bihata nîşandan û serê wê bihata girtin. Lê ez ê vê tiştê teqez qebûl nekim. Ez ji canê xwe jî bibim ez ê mafê keça xwe biparêzim û heta adalet bi cih were ez ê li pey vê dosyayê bim."


Kabaiş diyar kir ku ew li bendê rayedarên dewletê û Wezareta Dadê adalet pêk bîne û di heman demê de helwesta baroyan rexne kir û bal kişand ser hewldanên parêzerê xwe:


"Rayedarên dewletê jî dozger jî hema hema dizanin ka çi hatine serê vê zarokê. Dozgerên nû yên hatine tayînkirin dixebitin, em ji Wezareta Dadê bi bawerin, soz dan me. Wê di demeke nêz de em ê bi parêzerê xwe re berê biçin Wanê û piştre jî dîsa biçin Enqereyê, Wezareta Adaletê. Me ji baroyan bawer kir lê mixabin karên xwe baş nekirin, cesaret nekirin ku dosyayê aşkere bikin. Parêzerê malbata me pir baş dixebite. Xwezî ji destpêkê ve ev parêzerê me di nav kar de biba. Telefona keça min jî heta niha tam nehatiye vekirin; çû derveyî welat hat, niha jî ji Mêrsînê re hat şandin. Em li bendê ne ku ji wir agahî bên."


Kabaiş ku anî ziman ku berî deh rojan gef li wî hatiye xwarin û got, "ez ê tu carî dev jê bernedim"


Parêzer ji bo du gumanbaran biryara desteserkirinê xwest


Parêzerê malbatê Abdurrahman Karabulut, îmajên ku ji telefona Rojîn Kabaişê hatine bidestxistin ji pispor û zanyarên li hundir û derveyî welat re şandin.


Li gorî analîzên teknîkî yên ku ji aliyê pisporan ve hatine kirin ve, li ser sepanên medya civakî şopeke krîtîk bidest ketiye ku hatiye nirxandin yê yek ji gumanbaran e.


Li ser van daneyan, tomarên HTS û bazê yên telefona Rojîn Kabaişê dîsa bûn mijareke girîng ku bi baldarî bê lêkolînkirin. Di nirxandinên ku hatin kirin de diyar bû ku stasyonên bazê ku telefona Kabaişê di dema bûyerê de sînyal jê girtiye û telefonên du kesên ku xwediyê heman nav û paşnavî ne û weke gumanbar hatine nirxandin, di dema heman bûyerê de ji heman stasyonê sînyal dane.


Her weha di lêkolînan de li gorî daneyên hatin bidestxistin, yek ji gumanbaran hesaba xwe ya medya civakî yê ku tê nirxandin bi kar anîye girtiye.


Li ser van geşedanên şênber, parêzerê malbatê serî li Serdozgeriya Komarê ya Wanê da û daxwaz kir ku derbarê van herdû kesan de biryara desteserkirinê bidin û dest dayîne ser telefonên wan û nimûneyên wan ên DNAyê bigirin.


(EMK/AY)

author: Tom Midlane
title: Israel Is Treating Palestinian Children Flying Kites As an ‘Act of War’
content:
Israel has threatened to escalate attacks on Gaza and expel Palestinians from areas of the besieged and occupied enclave if children continue to fly paper kites.


Israeli defence minister Israel Katz said flying kites would be treated as “an act of war in every sense” and the IDF would retaliate “immediately and forcefully”. 


In a joint statement with Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday, Katz said: “A balloon is treated like a kite, and a kite is treated like a drone, with or without explosives.”


On the same day, Israeli air attacks on central Gaza killed at least three Palestinians, including a four-year-old child. 


A handful of kites have drifted into communities in the south of Israel over the last month,

 Al Jazeera reported

. None contained incendiary devices. 


The statement from Netanyahu and Katz also included a threat to “evacuate the population from areas from which kites, drones and balloons are launched”.


The UN slammed Israel’s response to children’s kites, with UN rights office spokesperson Ravina Shamdasani saying: “On the threat of expulsion due to children’s kite flying, I hope we can all agree that this is outrageous.” 


Popular committees in Gaza urged parents on Monday to discourage their children from flying kites “to protect their innocent lives”.


“Every summer, my kid, Ahmed, and the kids in the street fly those kites to entertain themselves,” Umm Mohammed, a mother in Gaza City,

told Reuters

. “But [now] I will not allow him to – not any more.”


Independent MP and former Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn wrote on X: “Israel has said that paper kites flown by Palestinian children will be treated as weapons of war. Read that again. 


“This is the reality of genocide: the total destruction of innocence, freedom and joy.”


At least

seven Palestinians have been killed

 and 10 wounded by Israeli attacks across Gaza in the last 24 hours.


The IDF shot a ten-year-old Palestinian girl, Amal Abu Khater, in the back as she sat in his displaced family’s tent in western Khan Younis, southern Gaza, eating her lunch,

Drop Site News reported

 on Monday.  


A relative of Amal said: “They were children playing with kites. They were just sitting there playing. They are killing children.”


Israel has killed at least 73,000 Palestinians and injured 174,000 since October 2023.

author: Andrés
title: La canción como latido de un pueblo
content:
Foto: Matias Sastre


Si se calla el cantor, calla la vida


porque la vida, la vida misma, es todo un canto


Si se calla el cantor, muere de espanto


la esperanza, la luz y la alegría


                                      

Horacio Guarany


Nacido al calor del estudio y la movilización social, el grupo musical

Todavía cantamos

 se presenta este sábado 29 de agosto en Fitzcarraldo club cultural a las 20.00. En entrevista, el grupo nos cuenta su historia: cómo a partir de la música y las letras del cancionero popular prohibido por la última dictadura militar argentina, sus canciones recorren la historia de la censura de aquellos años, pero también el valor de la resistencia y la memoria como formas de un compromiso que se actualiza cuando ante el poder de turno callar no parece ya una respuesta posible.

Por Marcos Gutiérrez para Anred.

 

  


Para ser coherentes a la hora de hablar de una conciencia colectiva,

Todavía cantamos

 ha respondido de forma colectiva la entrevista.


¿Cómo empezó el proyecto de este grupo y por qué tomaron esta temática de canciones prohibidas?


Todavía cantamos (TC): Somos un grupo de compañeros (y muchos amigos) estudiantes de la Tecnicatura de Música Popular de la UNLP que se dicta en la casa de las Madres de Plaza de Mayo. Desde que nos conocemos hemos buscado y encontrado muchísimas ocasiones para compartirnos desde nuestras sensibilidades, reivindicaciones y musicalidades. Plazas, casas, aulas, patios, calles, escenarios de nuestra escuela, de bibliotecas populares, de centros culturales, de marchas, que se convierten en fiesta, en peñas, en abrazos, en movilizaciones (en todas sus formas). Nuestra escuela nos enseña, entre otras cosas, a compartirnos y encontrarnos entre nosotrxs. Hemos hecho ciclos de cantautores y otros donde también interpretamos canciones prestadas que sentimos y necesitamos.


Todavía cantamos

 surgió gracias a una invitación y a una pregunta. Nos convocaron para participar de un ciclo en la Biblioteca Popular de Saavedra por los 50 años del golpe, llamado “¿Qué aprendimos y qué olvidamos desde entonces?” Esa pregunta dio vueltas y vueltas hasta que la mamá de una compañera nos dijo: “¿Y si hacen las canciones que estuvieron prohibidas?” Ahí se abrió todo un mundo en nuestras cotidianas juntadas. Comenzó a estar la lista del COMFER (Comité Federal de Radiodifusión). Nuestros instrumentos y un apasionante encuentro con lo que intentaron borrar: biografías, metáforas, sensaciones que despiertan, que tienen mucha data en cada detalle. De hecho, seguimos aun encontrándonos con estas obras y en contraparte vamos comprendiendo por qué les tenían tanto miedo.


 

¿Tuvieron alguna influencia de otros grupos similares o proyectos similares?


TC: Desde un principio supimos que esta búsqueda ya estuvo y está presente en nuestra sociedad desde los inicios de la censura. Hay artistas que interpretaron estas canciones-  Existe un disco hermoso que se llama “Canciones prohibidas” donde participan grandes músicos de acá: Fabi Cantilo, Palo Pandolfo, Gabo Ferro, Daniel Melero, Juan Falú…entre otros. Y por otro lado, “Todavía cantamos” es un proyecto que nos influye en la manera y en la voluntad de organizarnos es la asamblea de estudiantes de nuestra escuela.


 

¿Cuál fue el desafío más grande o dificultad que tuvieron o tienen como grupo?


TC: El desafío más grande, como el de todo proyecto actual (y al ser tantos) es coincidir en tiempo y espacio. Es el de todos los trabajadores y estudiantes de este momento histórico de tanta explotación. Así y todo lo conseguimos y lo fuimos construyendo milagrosamente en algunos recreos de nuestras cursadas, haciendo juntadas también por fuera donde pensamos para dónde vamos, cómo seguimos;  y le vamos dando forma, se van incorporando compas nuevos, de diversos años. Cada edición es diferente porque todo comenzó y sigue siendo un boca en boca. Le dedicamos tiempo a las canciones que hallamos, nos dejamos interpelar por ellas, las escuchamos, las estudiamos en todo su contexto y las hilamos en una narrativa que vamos descubriendo en todo este estudio y en el andar.


¿Más allá de la particularidad de ser canciones prohibidas cuáles son los requisitos para que entren en el listado de canciones que interpreta el grupo?


TC: En principio, tomar un relato como hilo conductor que articule diferentes temáticas ligadas a la censura, la ideología, la participación política, la libertad de expresión, la juventud despierta, la …

title: TFF'den Ziraat Türkiye Kupası değişikliği: 10+4 yabancı futbolcu kuralı uygulanmayacak
content:
Türkiye Futbol Federasyonu (TFF), kulüplerden gelen talepler doğrultusunda 2026-2027 Sezonu Ziraat Türkiye Kupası Müsabakaları Statüsü'nde değişiklik yaptı. Buna göre, TFF Ziraat Türkiye Kupası'nda kulüplerin belirlediği 10+4 yabancı futbolcu kuralının uygulanmayacağını duyurdu.

TFF tarafından yapılan açıklamada, kulüplerin belirledikleri 14 yabancı futbolcuyu yaşlarına bakılmaksızın oynatabilecekleri açıklandı. Konuyla ilgili, “Süper Lig ve Trendyol 1. Lig kulüpleri, A takım listesine yazamadıkları, Türkiye A Milli Futbol Takımı'nda oynama uygunluğuna sahip futbolcuları ve/veya yabancı uyruklu futbolcuları Ziraat Türkiye Kupası müsabakalarında oynatabileceklerdir. 10+4 yabancı futbolcu kuralı Ziraat Türkiye Kupası'nda uygulanmayacak ve kulüpler, belirledikleri 14 yabancı oyuncuyu yaşlarına bakılmaksızın oynatabileceklerdir. Trendyol Süper Lig kulüplerimiz, müsabaka isim listesine 14'ten fazla yabancı uyruklu futbolcu yazamayacaklardır. Trendyol 1. Lig ekiplerimiz ise sahada aynı anda en fazla 6 yabancı futbolcu bulundurmak koşuluyla müsabaka isim listesine en fazla 8 yabancı uyruklu futbolcu yazabileceklerdir. Düzenleme, kulüplerin mevcut kadrolarında bulunan oyuncular için geçerli olup, statü değişikliğinin yapıldığı 26.08.2026 tarihinden sonra kadroya dahil edilen oyuncular bu düzenlemeden yararlanamayacaktır” ifadelerine yer verildi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Unknown
title: Beşiktaş Başkanı Adalı’dan hakem tepkisi: “MHK Başkanı burada durduğu müddetçe Türk futbolu ileri gitmez”
content:
Fotoğraf: Zafer/Wikimedia Commons CC BY 4.0

Süper Lig’in 2. haftasında Corendon Alanyaspor’a 1-0 yenilen Beşiktaş’ta, maçta yaşanan hakem kararları gündemdeki yerini koruyor.

Beşiktaş Başkanı Serdal Adalı, TFF yönetimiyle görüşmek üzere Riva’daki Hasan Doğan Milli Takımlar Kamp ve Eğitim Tesisleri’ne gitti. Görüşmenin ardından açıklamalarda bulunan Adalı, özellikle Merkez Hakem Kurulu (MHK) Başkanı Ferhat Gündoğdu’yu hedef aldı.

Adalı, “Bu MHK Başkanı burada durduğu müddetçe maalesef Türk futbolu bir adım daha ileri gitmez” dedi.

Geçen hafta Fenerbahçe’nin, bu hafta ise Beşiktaş’ın hakem kararlarından mağdur olduğunu savunan Adalı, önümüzdeki haftalarda başka kulüplerin de benzer sorunlarla karşılaşacağını söyledi.

Alanyaspor-Beşiktaş maçında Fidan Aliti ile Leandro Trossard arasında yaşanan fiziksel temas ve pozisyonun ardından hakem Adnan Deniz Kayatepe ile VAR hakemi Bülent Birincioğlu’na tepki gösteren Adalı, yaşananları “rezillik” olarak nitelendirdi.

Adalı, “O tokat olayıyla ilgili söylenecek tek bir kelime bulamıyorum.” ifadelerini kullandı.

VAR hakeminin pozisyonu görmesine rağmen müdahale etmemesini eleştiren Adalı, kararın iyi niyetli olmadığını savundu.

Adalı, yalnızca Beşiktaş’ın değil, alt liglerde mücadele eden kulüplerin de hakem yönetimlerinden şikayetçi olduğunu ileri sürdü.

Son iki günde Süper Lig, 1. Lig ve 2. Lig’den 30-35 kulüp başkanının kendisini aradığını belirten Adalı, sorunun daha geniş olduğunu söyledi.

TFF Başkanı ve yönetiminin MHK Başkanı konusunda gereken adımı atamadığını savunan Adalı, konuyu Cumhurbaşkanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan’a taşıyacağını açıkladı.

Adalı, “Randevu isteyeceğim ve hakemlerin bulunduğu durumu Sayın Cumhurbaşkanı’mıza da arz edeceğim.” dedi.

Beşiktaş Başkanı, Fenerbahçe ile oynanacak derbide yabancı VAR hakemi talep edeceklerini de açıkladı.

Bu konuda Fenerbahçe yönetimiyle görüşeceklerini belirten Adalı, sarı-lacivertli kulübün de talebi desteklemesi halinde federasyondan yabancı VAR hakemi isteyeceklerini söyledi.

Adalı, “Fenerbahçe de ‘evet’ derse yabancı VAR talebimiz var.” diye konuştu.

Adalı, maçta yaşanan pozisyonun futbolcular üzerindeki etkisine de dikkat çekti.

Leandro Trossard’ın olayın ardından psikolojik olarak zorlandığını belirten Adalı, “Trossard’ın 3 gündür psikolojisini düzeltmeye çalışıyoruz.” dedi.

Yaşananların yalnızca Beşiktaş’ı ilgilendirmediğini söyleyen Adalı, benzer olayların Galatasaray, Fenerbahçe veya Trabzonspor’un da başına gelebileceğini ifade etti.

TFF yönetiminin söz konusu pozisyonda hakem kararının hatalı olduğunu kabul ettiğini ileri süren Adalı, buna rağmen MHK Başkanı’nın görevde kalmasını eleştirdi.

Kulüplerin transfer ve kadro yapılanmalarına milyonlarca avro harcadığını belirten Adalı, hakem kararlarının kulüplerin geleceğini etkilediğini söyledi.

Adalı, “Bilgisiz bir adamın iki dudağının arasında koskoca camiaların kaderi belirlenecek.” diyerek MHK Başkanı’na yönelik eleştirilerini sürdürdü.

Beşiktaş Başkanı, MHK Başkanı’nın görevden alınamamasının arkasında “başka bir güç” olduğunu düşündüğünü belirterek açıklamalarını tamamladı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: AKP’li Menemen Belediyesi’nde festivale para var işçi alacağına yok
content:
İzmir- AKP’li Menemen Belediye Başkanı Aydın Pehlivan, göreve geldikten sonra taşınmaz satışları ve usulsüz imar uygulamalarıyla gündemdeki yerini koruyor. Menemen Belediyesi, işten çıkardığı işçilerin tazminat, mesai ve yasal haklarından doğan alacaklarını mahkeme kararlarına rağmen ödememekte ısrar ederken festivallere para harcamaya devam ediyor.

Menemen Belediyesi'nin, Temmuz 2026 Meclis toplantısında meclis üyelerini karşı karşıya getiren işçi alacakları, AKP Grup Sözcüsü Dilaver Kişili'nin “Ödenmeyen işçi alacağı yok” iddiasına alacaklarını tahsil edemeyen işçiler tepki göstermişti. Menemen Belediyesi’nde işten atılan işçiler haklarının ödenmemesine karşılık haciz işlemi başlatmışlardı. İsçiler 2 Eylül'de alacaklarına karşılık belediye mallarını haczetmeye hazırlanıyor.

2024 yerel seçimlerinin hemen ardından işten çıkarıldığını belirten Erdinç Yılmaz, “Bu kadar konser, festival yapan Menemen Belediyesi yaklaşık iki buçuk yıl önce işten çıkararak mağdur ettiği yetmiyormuş gibi haklarımızı da vermiyor. Dava açtık kazandık, alacaklarımız olan, tazminatlarımızı mahkeme kararımız olmasına rağmen ödememekte ısrar ediyor” dedi.

Yılmaz, “Satışa çıkardığı hatta satıp tapu devrini yaptığı arsalarda haczimiz olmasına rağmen alacaklarımız ödenmedi. Üstelik temmuz ayı meclis toplantısında AKP'li Menemen ve İzmir Büyükşehir Belediyesi Meclis Üyesi Dilaver Kişili, Menemen halkının ve toplantıdaki Meclis Üyelerinin, biz emekçilerin gözlerinin içine bakarak yalan söyledi. 2 Eylül 2026 tarihinde Belediyenin mallarına icra yoluyla haciz etmek için işlem başlattık” diye konuştu.

Haksız yere sorgusuz sualsiz işten atıldıklarını belirten adının açıklanmasını istemeyen bir işçi, “Aydın Pehlivan, seçim öncesi kimseyi işten atmayacağını vaat ediyordu. Seçim bitti vaatler unutuldu. Dava açtık, davayı kazandık şimdi de paramızı ödemiyorlar. Festivaller için milyonlarca lira para harcayan Aydın Pehlivan elini vicdanına koy hakkımızı öde” dedi.

Adının açıklanmasını istemeyen diğer işçi ise “23 Ağustos’ta yapılan Bozalan İncir Festivali konserlerinde şarkıcılara ödenen para yerine öncelikle bizim hakkımız ödenmeliydi. Festivale karşı değiliz fakat belediye bütçesinin öncelikle işçi alacaklarına ayrılmasından yanayız. 2,5 yıldır süren mağduriyetimiz son bulsun” dedi.

Yüksek maliyetli festivaller düzenleyen AKP’li Menemen Belediyesi’ne bir tepki de İzmir Büyükşehir ve Menemen Belediyesi Yeni Parti Meclis Üyesi Erdal Karagöz’den geldi.

Karagöz, “Emekçi kardeşlerimizin hak etmiş oldukları tazminatlarının biran önce ödenmesi gerekmektedir. Ev kirasını elektrik ve su ücretlerini ödeyemeyen arkadaşlarımız var. Hasta olan babasına hasta yatağı alamayan işçi kızımızın acısı var. Bunlar Aydın Pehlivan’ın aklına gelmiyor. Önce işçi arkadaşlarımızın hak kayıpları karşılanmalı ardından festivallere bütçe ayrılmalıdır” dedi.

Menemen Belediye Başkanı Aydın Pehlivan, 2024 yılı sonunda yaptığı açıklamada, düzenlenen 47 konserin her şey dahil maliyetinin ortalama 1,9 milyon TL olduğunu belirtmişti. Buna karşılık muhalefet partileri ve çeşitli kaynaklar, 2023 ile 2024-2025 yılları arasındaki şatafatlı festival, konser ve organizasyon giderlerinin (İbrahim Tatlıses, Ajda Pekkan, Gülben Ergen ve Simge Sağın gibi sanatçıların katıldığı etkinlikler dahil) milyonlarca lirayı bulduğunu ve bütçede büyük sapmalara yol açtığını iddia ediyor.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Unknown
title: More Kurdish citizens arrested in Iran
content:
Iranian Ministry of Intelligence forces have arrested Kurdish citizens Sanan Farasati, Saadoun Dastari and Rahman Azarakhsh in Oshnavieh, West Azerbaijan Province, taking them to undisclosed locations.


The Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) has reported that, in the early hours of 24 August, intelligence agents arrested Dastari, from the village of Hassan Nuran, and Azarakhsh, from the village of Sufian in Oshnavieh County, without warrants.


The previous day, Ministry of Intelligence forces arrested Farasati at his family home in Oshnavieh.


No information is yet available regarding the reasons for the arrests or the charges brought against the three men.


Despite repeated enquiries by their families, security and judicial authorities have refused to provide any information about their situation.

author: Unknown
title: After nine years, families visit the destroyed cemetery of guerrillas in Besta
content:
After nine years, relatives have visited the Şehîd Rojat and Şehîd Zelal Cemetery in the Besta region in Şırnak province for the first time. The cemetery contains the graves of fallen members of the People’s Defence Forces (HPG) and the Free Women’s Troops (YJA Star). The site was bombed from the air in 2017 and subsequently largely destroyed. The Turkish state then designated the area a “military security zone” and restricted access for years.


Together with the local branch of MEBYA-DER (Association for Solidarity, Cooperation and Culture of Families Who Have Lost Relatives in the Cradle of Civilizations), family members were able to reach the graves for the first time in years. Among them were relatives of Niyazi Akın (Şervan Sasun), Abdurgani Yanar (Celal Çeli), and Abdurahman Erkan (Koçero Kurdo), who lost their lives in Besta on May 17, 2009. Sultan Erkan, Memet Metin Erkan, Emine Özkan, and Neslihan Akın set out to search for their relatives’ graves for the first time in years.


Searching for the names of their relatives


At the site, the families found the cemetery largely destroyed. Numerous gravestones had been broken or toppled. Among the rubble, families searched for stones on which the names of their fallen family members could still be identified. The families cleaned and kissed the gravestones they found. They then commemorated their relatives and offered prayers.


“Every person has their land, their cemetery. How could this place have been brought to such a state?” Emine Özkan said, reacting to the destruction. “All over the world, people’s graves are protected. When we arrived here, we saw that the cemetery had been completely destroyed.”


She called for the destruction not to be accepted as irreversible: “Hopefully, it will not remain like this. People’s graves and their land must be respected.”


“This is an injustice”


MEBYA-DER board member Fahrettin Salgucak also criticized the condition of the cemetery. Although the destruction had already been known, the full extent of the damage became apparent once again during the latest visit, he said.


“This is our cemetery for the martyrs. We had already seen that it had been destroyed. When we returned today, we saw that everything around the cemetery had been devastated in the worst possible way,” Salgucak said.


Salgucak added that even reaching the graves had been extremely difficult for the families. “This is an injustice. Such a thing is unacceptable in Islam as well,” Salgucak stated.
